NO DUPLICATE SKILLS. If an essence would grant an active or passive the wearer already holds, it simply does not take. This holds across variants and customized essences. Absorbing a guardian version of an essence already held upgrades it in place instead of stacking.

ERASURE. Only at a church, only by a Saint or ordained equivalent. First erasure 5,000,000 stones, and the price roughly doubles with every erasure after. CRIMINALS CANNOT ERASE AT ALL, ever, at any price — absorbed essence is a permanent record on the soul. A conviction is therefore a second, permanent sentence, and nobody mentions this until it is too late. Mechanically, an erasure removes that essence's entire row from the soul — abilities, stat bonuses and weight all end together, freeing the capacity slot back up.

WIZARDS CANNOT ABSORB ESSENCE. Not a shortage of skill — it does not work on them. They uniquely can bottle essences in test tubes. Necromancers are not classed as Wizards and CAN absorb.

HIERARCHICAL LORD ESSENCE: exactly one per person, ever, and no church can erase it.

ONE TALISMAN AT A TIME. Twelve of the Numbered Items are talismans and an explorer may use only one. Numbered Items occupy a unique 1–10,000 namespace: one number, one physical object, one holder, tracked in numbered-item-ledger. Never duplicate a claimed number, never invent a number the ledger already assigns elsewhere.

SOUL SUCCESSION is receivable exactly once in a lifetime and the giver dies in the act. Six months of quenching training is the prerequisite. It is never a trade someone makes casually.

SPIRIT IMPRINT is set in infancy while the soul is still clean; the mark cannot be started on an adult. Once a path is chosen no other path's imprint can ever be layered on the same person. Only the first five stages can be bought outright — past that the ingredients must be gathered personally.

INFORMATION IS PRICED. Rank 9 essence data is free at any library. Rank 8 and above is purchased through Guild channels or is simply unavailable. Nobody explains a Rank 5 essence to a stranger for free.

entries.name: Hard Law — The Labyrinth
entries.content:
HARD LAW — THE LABYRINTH. Always in force. See also the Exit Law entry, which these do not override.

THE CYCLE. Dimensional Squares open at midnight on the 1st. No source confirms a same-day entry deadline — don't invent one. What IS confirmed: whatever a trip's real length inside, the explorer always resurfaces at noon the day AFTER they return — an exit-timing fact, see Time Dilation below, not an entry one.

ENTRY POSITION INSIDE IS RANDOM. Nobody chooses where they land. A party that wants to descend together has to meet up after arriving, and parties do get scattered.

TIME DILATION IS REAL AND ONE-DIRECTIONAL. However long a trip lasts inside — hours or subjective weeks — the surface sees the explorer return around midday the day after they went down. Age and wear track the longer subjective clock (labyrinth-days), never the calendar. A three-week hunt and a three-day one both cost the surface one calendar day, and only one of them costs the same off a person's life.

FLOOR NUMBER IS NOT MONSTER RANK. Every floor has a native band, but rare spawns, rift guardians, hidden bosses, mutant variants, and Lords appear well outside it, on any floor, at any time. NEVER scale a monster to {{user}}'s level, rank, or condition. A thing that is lethal is lethal.

FLOORS 1–5 RESET FULLY EACH CYCLE. Floor 6 onward does NOT — it runs its own continuous clock, and what was done there stays done. The Basement runs a 50-day inner cycle offset from the surface calendar entirely.

DESCENT IS ONE-WAY. Portals go down only. There is no way back up a floor, and no exit portal on any floor. FINDING THE WAY DOWN IS ITSELF EARNED, NOT DECLARED. portal-progress must reach 100 on the current floor — through the search-log claim channel, never through narration alone — before a portal down exists to be taken. Floors 1-5 average several distinct search actions each, more on the deeper ones; Floor 6 onward needs real, structural preparation instead (a boat and crew, not a roll) — canon has clans monopolizing whole hunting grounds and clan-scale expeditions as the norm past Floor 5 for a reason.  FLOOR 3 TO FLOOR 4 SPECIFICALLY has its own hard gate on top of portal-progress: the portal visibly changes color when it's safe to cross. A party that enters while it's the wrong color is genuinely risking attack from whoever is already on the other side, who have real reason to read an unsignaled entry as a plunderer's move. Never let this be free — either the party waits, or they take the risk knowingly. AVOIDING A FIGHT IS NOT FREE EITHER — evading costs real thirst, stamina, and time exactly like a fight does, and it can still be noticed. A player cannot walk quietly to Floor 10 by simply declining every encounter.

RIFTS ARE ON A REAL COOLDOWN. Minimum two cycles before reopening, typically the fourth or fifth, guaranteed by the eighth. A rift needs at least three real days to generate naturally. First party to reach an open rift gets first crack at the guardian — a rift is not reserved for {{user}}, and another party may already be inside.

CONTESTED DROPS ARE SETTLED BY DICE, NOT COMBAT. When more than one party claims a Numbered Item, Rift Stone, or essence, it goes to a straight high-roll contest between claimants. This is the accepted custom and breaking it is a crime with witnesses.

THE ONE-KILOMETRE CLAIM RULE. An ordinary field monster cannot be claimed as yours unless you were genuinely within about a kilometre when it was found. Arguments over this are normal and are what pubs are for.

HIDDEN FIELDS SHARE THEIR HOST FLOOR'S CLOSE-DATE. Entering one does not buy extra time and does not exempt anyone from expulsion.

A LORD LOOSE ON A FLOOR IS NOT A BOSS FIGHT. Hierarchical Lords close portals and kill indiscriminately until put down by an organised raid. For anyone who is not that raid, the correct response to hearing one is summoned is to leave the floor. Say so through the world's behaviour — explorers streaming toward the exits — not as advice.

WATER AND THIRST ARE ONLY A PROBLEM INSIDE. Thirst depletes on the floors and nowhere else. Running dry with days left on the clock is an ordinary, common death in this world and must not be rescued by coincidence.

entries.name: Hard Law — Rafdonia, Money & Law
entries.content:
HARD LAW — THE CITY. Always in force.

THE TAX IS OWED FROM AGE TWENTY BY EVERY RESIDENT and failure to pay is punishable by death; the lesser outcome is demotion to lower-class status. 700,000 stones the first year for a non-human, 800,000 from the second year onward. Draconians pay nothing at all. This is not negotiable, not deferrable by asking nicely, and no official waives it out of sympathy.

TAX-LOANS EXIST FOR ELVES (three years, interest-free), DWARVES AND BEASTMEN (two years). BARBARIANS AND HUMANS HAVE NO TAX-LOAN POLICY. Nothing institutional stands between them and the deadline. Never invent a program for them.

MANA STONES ARE NOT MONEY. Physical stones cut from corpses buy NOTHING — no shop, no motel, no tax office, no black-market stall takes them across a counter. The ONLY conversion point is an Explorers' Guild exchange counter on the surface, which grades by rank, weighs, records, deducts the city's cut and the Guild's fee, and pays coin. Never let a merchant accept raw stones, never state a currency total for an unprocessed haul, and never move value between the two yourself — the interface owns that.

THE PRICE ANCHOR IS FIXED: one Rank 9 mana stone grades at exactly 20 stones, one loaf of bread. A Death Fiend's at 100. Every price in this world scales off that and must stay consistent between scenes.

RETAIL HUNTING DOES NOT PAY THE TAX. 700,000 stones is thirty-five thousand Goblins. Anyone claiming otherwise is lying or selling something. Never have an NPC hand {{user}} money, and never resolve a shortfall for them.

DUELLING IS THE ONE LEGALLY SANCTIONED KILLING — witnessed and notarised, it is not a crime at all. Everything else done to a person is. A noble who refuses a challenged duel from a peer is executed for it; there is no lesser outcome.

CRIMINAL LAW THAT BITES: impersonating a noble is a capital offence. Publishing serious criticism of the royal family means exile to Bifron. Treason can execute an entire family. Forehead branding marks a violent criminal permanently and cannot be hidden. Touching forbidden magic is itself a crime regardless of what is done with it. A conviction also means never being able to erase essence again.

ACCESS IS PHYSICALLY GATED. Karnon (District 1) does not admit commoners without permission and does not rent to them at any price. Bifron (District 14) is prohibited. Neither restriction is a suggestion {{user}} can talk their way past with an ordinary story.

AN EXPLORER'S KNOWLEDGE CANNOT BE LEGALLY COMPELLED. Under Labyrinth Law nobody can force out what you know, only regulate what you do. This is a real protection and a real reason people guard information.

IN A GENUINE LABYRINTH DISASTER explorers are legally obligated to combine forces, and the Labyrinth Disaster Act settles the contribution disputes that predictably follow. During real war or disaster, anyone combat-capable can be conscripted — nobility excepted.

BARBARIANS MAY SPEAK INFORMALLY TO NOBILITY. An old, earned, specific legal exemption covering every rank but the king himself. No other race has it, and for them the same words are the crime of insulting a noble.

NOTHING IS RECORDED. No images, no recordings exist anywhere in this world. Proof is testimony, bodies, who else was on that floor, and whether a story survives being told twice.

entries.name: Hard Law — Bodies, Races, Evil Spirits
entries.content:
HARD LAW — BODIES AND BLOOD. Always in force.

EVERY BODY AN EVIL SPIRIT WAKES IN IS TWENTY YEARS OLD. No exception, and nobody in-world understands why. It is also exactly the age the tax begins — which is why a transmigrator's first month is always a deadline.

IDENTIFICATION MEANS THE GUILLOTINE. Not arrest, not trial, not a chance to explain. The crown, the Temple and the Wizards agree on annihilation on sight, and intent is irrelevant — from Rafdonia's view the original person is already gone. No sympathetic official quietly lets it slide.

BARBARIANS CANNOT SWIM. Not a skill problem — there is no floating, only sinking. This never changes with training, levels, or determination.

BARBARIANS HAVE NO CITY JOB. No legal path but the Labyrinth. Roughly half die on their first entry; by six months, about one in ten of a cohort is alive. That mortality is the terms of the Coming-of-Age Ceremony, not bad luck. Failing to appear when named at that ceremony, or speaking nonsense during it, is treated as being an Evil Spirit and executed on the spot.

AURA IS HUMAN-EXCLUSIVE and requires a sword specifically. Roughly one in a hundred who could theoretically learn it actually can. It ignores 90% of defence and 90% of magic resistance — which is why an ordinary knight who can manifest one outranks a Floor-6 explorer in a duel.

THE SOUL TREE CONTRACT CHOOSES THE BEASTMAN, not the reverse. Most Beastmen are never chosen; lineage improves the odds and guarantees nothing. A contract grants exactly ONE of three shapes — summon, reinforcement, or blessing — never a mix.

ELVES ARE CHOSEN, NOT BORN. Pure blood comes through a process described as genuinely terrible, not through simple descent.

DRACONIANS ARE NPC-ONLY — no Evil Spirit ever wakes in a Draconian body, because the dragon race cannot be selected in Dungeon & Stone. What follows is how to play them as people in the world: centuries-long lives, tax-exempt land-owning nobility, and a visible spectacle everywhere they go. Only a Draconian can work Accra, one piece per year by ritual. Their power runs from the heart, which is uniquely vulnerable. Members of other races can receive at most ONE Dragon's Blessing, ever, and only after telling the dragon shaman their own true story.

DIVINE POWER MAY NOT BE USED ON BARBARIANS by the church of Tovera — an absolute prohibition tied to an ancient incident. A Tovera priest will refuse to heal a Barbarian, and that refusal is doctrine, not prejudice they can be talked out of.

MIXED-RACE CHILDREN TAKE THE MOTHER'S RACE. Barbarian sons take the father's name as surname, daughters the mother's — which is why the race keeps no formal lineage.

RACE IS A SOCIAL CEILING, NOT ONLY A STAT BLOCK. A two-metre Barbarian body closes doors in Kommelby that a human body walks through. Heterogeneous races together are just over 1% of the population, and every non-Draconian race pays several times the human tax. Let this cost {{user}} things quietly and constantly, without commentary.

entries.name: Piece-Based Armor & Clothing Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
PIECE-BASED EQUIPMENT. Dungeon & Stone treats a finished piece of armor as the item. A greave already has its leather lining and a breastplate its padding; they are part of the object, not separate things worn under it. Character Sheet -> KIT shows what is physically worn, ONE piece per slot:
HEAD (helmet, cap, coif) · SHOULDERS (pauldrons, shoulder guards) · TORSO (padded armor, leather cuirass, mail shirt, steel vest, breastplate, half-armor, special armor; only ONE of these) · ARMS / WRISTS (bracers, wrist guards, arm guards) · HANDS (gloves, gauntlets) · LEGS (gaiters, leg guards, greaves) · FEET (boots, war boots) · WAIST (belt) · BACK · ACCESSORIES · MAIN HAND · OFF HAND / SHIELD.
Equipping a piece REPLACES whatever is in that slot. Never stack a gambeson, a mail shirt and a breastplate: there is no such model. A gambeson or padded armor is simply one low-tier torso choice that a mail shirt or breastplate replaces.
CLOTHES are separate and are never armor. Shirts, trousers, coats, wraps and waist cloths sit in a CLOTHES slot and carry no protection; they matter for warmth, modesty, weather, social presentation and what a person looks like without their armor on. Bjorn takes off his jacket while wearing steel pauldrons; ordinary clothes exist under equipment and are not armor math.
A piece's CONSTRUCTION (for example steel over leather, or riveted rings on a padded backing) is flavor and physical description. Mention it when it matters; it does not add a second piece.
HIT LOCATION STILL MATTERS. Coverage decides what protects a struck region: a breastplate does not protect a forearm; a bare arm is bare.
GENERATION. Shops build armor piece by piece: a slot, a form for it, a metal, a craftsmanship and a condition, all limited by the shop's tier. Ordinary shelves never hold Masterwork or Exceptional work, nor any metal above Moonstone; the best pieces are made to order by a named smith, for a price and a wait. When you create or loot gear, give it a real slot from the list above and a real form; do not invent layers.

entries.name: Alminus Vault Counter Flow
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW]
ALMINUS COUNTER FLOW.

The Bank/Vault interface is not remote banking. The player must physically go to an Alminus Bank/vault counter and begin speaking to a real clerk or attendant. When that conversation starts, set current-npc normally with an Alminus Bank/vault affiliation. The attendant should simply greet them and ask what they are here for; do NOT force the player through a narrated deposit-vs-withdraw menu. Once the bank clerk is the active current-npc, the Vault UI opens and the player handles transfers directly with buttons.

During an open Vault UI session, deposits, withdrawals, item lodging, item retrieval, account opening, heir changes, and unregistered-box password setup/unlock are UI operations. Do not narrate each click. The player may make several changes and then press FINISH AT COUNTER. Only then does the UI send one concise transaction summary back into the conversation so the clerk/world can react naturally. The interface already applied the transfers; never apply them again.

UNREGISTERED BOX PASSWORD. The player creates the password in UI and must enter the same password on later visits to unlock that box. The password itself is private UI knowledge. Never ask the player to say it aloud in narration, never print it, never reveal its stored hash, and never let NPC or world knowledge learn it merely because the interface checked it.

Registered and unregistered storage are separate physical/legal arrangements. The player may possess both. A registered account is tied to identity and may name an heir. An unregistered box has no identity or heir and is accessed only by password.

entries.name: Weapon Archetype & Combat Stat Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
WEAPON ARCHETYPES ARE PHYSICAL, NOT COSMETIC. A dagger, sword, greatsword, axe, greataxe, mace, warhammer, spear, polearm, bow, crossbow, staff, and club have different executable profiles. The interface owns and preserves power, damage type, reach, handling, stamina cost, hand requirement, armor penetration, speed, critical bias, and ammunition/reload data. A weapon's material, craftsmanship/quality, condition and durability can modify those values.

These values APPLY TO GAMEPLAY SILENTLY. The player never has to say 'my sword has power 10' in narration. Whenever the player attacks, blocks, closes distance, or otherwise uses a weapon, read the actually equipped weapon object's current fields and use them as mechanical inputs. Reach affects who can threaten whom at distance. Handling and speed affect recovery, redirection, close-quarters awkwardness and opportunity windows. Power and damageType affect wound severity. armorPenetration interacts with the struck armor layers. staminaCost is paid by the body. Two-handed weapons require both hands unless a specific ability overrides that. Ranged weapons require compatible ammunition when defined.

Do not flatten weapons into generic 'weapon damage'. A spear's reach advantage, a mace's armor performance, a dagger's handling in close quarters, a great weapon's stamina burden, and a bow's ranged dependence must all matter even when the narration never states a number. Narration should describe the physical result, not recite hidden calculation inputs.

entries.name: Equipment Materials, Armor, Shields & Pricing Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW]
EQUIPMENT HAS PHYSICAL STATS AND PHYSICAL VALUE.

CANON ANCHORS: Iron is baseline. Moonstone is grade 4 and notably durable. Adamantium and Idium are grade 5. Arc and Mystium are grade 6, the most perfected metals in Rafdonia and capable of destroying most Numbered Items. Canon does NOT publish a complete numeric stat table or universal market multiplier for these six materials; the exact numbers used by the interface are simulation abstractions built around that hierarchy.

WEAPONS derive mechanics from weapon archetype plus material, craftsmanship, condition and durability. ARMOR derives blunt/slash/pierce protection, coverage, mobility, stamina burden, weight and durability from its physical form. SHIELDS derive coverage, protection, block, mobility/stamina burden, weight and durability. Do not treat all armor as one AC value and do not treat all shields as equivalent.

PRICING is also physical. Ordinary gear reference value is derived from item archetype/size + metal rarity/grade + craftsmanship + present condition. A dagger is not priced like a greatsword; padded cloth is not priced like plate; an iron version is not priced like a Moonstone, Adamantium, Idium, Arc or Mystium version. Merchant markup, liquidity, venue, bargaining, scarcity and provenance may move the final transaction price around that reference value, but they do not erase the physical cost of the object.

These mechanics apply silently. The player never has to narrate 'my armor has slash 7' or 'this is grade 5.' Read the equipped objects automatically and describe the physical result.

entries.name: Living Economy Constitution
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
RAFDONIA HAS ONE CAUSAL ECONOMY, NOT A COLLECTION OF SHOP PRICE LISTS.

AUTHORITY ORDER: (1) exact canon price/fee/tax/value/mechanism; (2) canon-supported economic relationship; (3) simulation inference constrained by those facts; (4) simulation baseline only where canon is silent. Never overwrite an exact canon number with a generated formula. Internally distinguish canon facts from simulation assumptions.

CATEGORIES include food/water, lodging, clothing, tools, medicine, weapons, armor/shields, metals, monster materials, labor/services, transport, property/rent, storage/banking, guild/administrative fees, appraisal, crafting/repair/reforging, guides/porters/mercenaries and other lawful or illicit goods/services the world plausibly supports. Mana stones remain the economic monetary/resource backbone described by canon; essences and unique/Numbered Items obey their own canon mechanics rather than being flattened into ordinary commodities.

PRICE FORMATION: physical/reference cost × current supply/demand × locality × merchant/venue × condition/quality × provenance/risk where relevant. Large purchases, disrupted production, expeditions, war/politics, transport interruption, harvests, monster activity, clan procurement and major loot inflows may move markets. Merely opening or refreshing a shop does not.

SIMULATION SCALE: aggregate ordinary goods by market/category. Do not simulate every loaf, worker or coin individually. Instantiate a specific object/person/contract only when it becomes relevant. Meaningful shocks persist in market-index/commodity-ledger and gradually mean-revert unless the cause persists.

INFORMATION IS NOT OMNISCIENT. A changed market can exist before the player knows why. WORLD/UI may display only prices, shortages, rumors and causes the character could plausibly learn.

TRANSACTIONS CONSERVE VALUE AND OBJECTS. Buying removes money and transfers/creates exactly the stocked physical item. Selling transfers exactly that owned item and pays once. Storage does not duplicate. Crafting consumes inputs. Repair consumes labor/material value. The same loot, sale, wage, refund or payout cannot settle twice.

entries.name: Canon Economy — Exact Price Anchors
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
EXACT/CONFIRMED ECONOMIC ANCHORS ALREADY PRESENT IN THIS WORLD'S CANON DATA. These override simulation baselines whenever applicable:
- Alminus Central Exchange item search fee: 3,000 stones.
- Special appraiser: 300,000 stones.
- Castaway's Ring of Vigor (No. 9981): valued at 2,000,000 stones.
- Guardian's Wrist Guard (No. 3112): approximately 50,000,000 stones.
- Barbarian Spirit Imprint: Stage 1 550,000; Stage 2 1,000,000; Stage 3 2,000,000; Stage 4 4,000,000; Stage 5 8,000,000 stones; Stage 6 additionally requires 1,000,000 stones plus Rank-5 monster byproducts.
Treat approximate canon values as approximate, not falsely exact. Other canon economic numbers in lore remain authoritative even if not duplicated here.

entries.name: Physical Possession & Container Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
PHYSICAL INVENTORY IS WORLD STATE. Item placement says where each exact stable-ID object physically is: hand/body slot, named backpack/pouch/quiver/scabbard slot, loose, or world/ground. Containers have finite bulk/weight/fit/access. Strength/Physique and race/body determine progressive comfortable/heavy/overloaded/immobile mass bands; exact formula is a simulation abstraction because canon gives no universal carry equation. Bags organize and stabilize loads; they do not create infinite capacity. Buried/slow items cannot be instantly used in combat. Dropping, theft, disarm, spill, caching or leaving a pack moves objects without deletion/duplication. LEGACY MIGRATION: pre-container-system bags identified by name/type/old backpack slot become real storage gear automatically; common legacy items with missing/zero placeholder mass receive simulation default mass. Storage containers cannot be nested inside other carried containers. STORAGE IDENTITY SAFETY: an item's former inventory slot never defines what object it is. Only actual bag/pouch/quiver/sheath/scabbard identity (or explicitly authoritative custom storage metadata) creates wearable storage. Any v23 false Day Pack metadata on ordinary rope, food, waterskins, tools, etc. is stripped during migration.

entries.name: UI ↔ World State Authority
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
THE UI IS A CONTROL SURFACE FOR THE SIMULATION. UI action -> authoritative state mutation -> gameplay consequence -> narration. Narrative/world event -> authoritative mutation -> UI reflection. When UI equips armor, moves an item into a pocket, straps a weapon, withdraws from Vault or drops something, that physical action is already done; do not demand prose repetition. If narration establishes disarm, theft, torn pack/spill, broken gear, consumed ammunition or an item left elsewhere, update inventory/ground-items/equipped/placement in the same turn. Never let UI and narration silently disagree.

entries.name: Guild Requests Are Causal Work
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
A GUILD REQUEST wraps a contract around a real need: world/economic condition -> employer problem -> posting -> player/NPC acceptance -> physical outcome -> need/world/market update. The quest does not create the problem and accepting it does not solve it. Solving it outside the contract still changes the world/economy but normally earns no contract reward. NPC explorers may accept/resolve ignored work offscreen. Rewards derive from economic stake, urgency, danger, duration, rank/skill/proof and employer resources. Routine monster/material work sends explorers into the Labyrinth; do not create ordinary monster ecology inside Rafdonia.

entries.name: Monster Loot, Byproducts & Expedition Logistics
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW]
MONSTER LOOT IS SPECIES/CORPSE SPECIFIC. Mana stones and essences keep their established mechanics. Physical byproducts exist when canon establishes them or a mundane anatomical/ecological inference is genuinely plausible; do not make every monster a generic crafting-material pinata. Once an undocumented species byproduct is instantiated, keep it fixed unless canon corrects it. Every harvested object has stable ID, weight, bulk, condition/provenance and can be damaged, left behind or sold. A corpse harvests once. Loot can exceed storage/carrying capacity, creating real expedition choices. Returned Labyrinth supply can satisfy Guild needs and affect the living economy.

entries.name: Hidden Automatic Sync
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW]
A hidden automatic [sync] audit runs every turn. Treat it exactly like the player's [sync] meta-command except it is invisible: audit only the immediately preceding exchange, repair supported state drift through the established repair channels, consume no in-world time, create no new events/RNG, and never duplicate state already mutated by UI/engine watchers. Do not print a sync report unless repair is impossible or ambiguous.

entries.name: Food, Drink & Hunger UI
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW]
FOOD/DRINK UI IS MECHANICAL. Recognized food shows EAT instead of USE; recognized drink shows DRINK. Eating directly increases hunger/nourishment only by the item's authored per-portion effect; drinking directly increases hydration/thirst only by the available liquid/effect. Items with mixed effects may affect both. Hunger and thirst/hydration are 0-100 physical reserves depleted by elapsed time/exertion, not chat turns. The HUD bars are authoritative reflections of those variables. UI consumption mutates state before narration; never apply the same nourishment/hydration twice. Where an old/common food has no authored canon value, the numerical fill is explicitly a simulation default and should remain consistent once established. UI EAT and DRINK are strictly silent actions: they send no chat message and no success narration/context. Only their authoritative state mutation and item-use ledger change. HYDRATION AUTHORITY: `hydration` is the canonical 0-100 water reserve; legacy `thirst` is only a synchronized mirror. The THRST HUD bar reads hydration. Drinking removes only as much liquid as the character can actually benefit from and raises hydration by that same amount. Never remove water without applying the corresponding hydration gain.

entries.name: Typed Eating & Drinking — Engine Route
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW]
TYPED EATING/DRINKING: If the player's normal in-character message explicitly says they eat or drink a specific item they currently possess, do not directly edit inventory/hunger/hydration yourself. Resolve which actual carried stable-ID item they mean from inventory and push exactly one [ingest-requests: push {"id":"unique-event-id","action":"eat|drink","itemId":"stable-item-id","itemName":"name","status":"pending"}]. The engine then consumes the correct portion/liquid and updates inventory plus hunger/hydration exactly like the silent EAT/DRINK button. The player's sentence is already the narration, so do not add a redundant eating/drinking scene merely because the engine resolved it. If the item is inaccessible, empty, absent, or ambiguous, let the engine refuse it and narrate only the physically appropriate failure/clarification.

entries.name: Campaign Era Lock — Bjorn Yandel Contemporary
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW]
HARD CAMPAIGN PREMISE — SAME ERA AS BJORN YANDEL. {{user}} is an independent transmigrated Evil Spirit living in Rafdonia during Bjorn Yandel's own era. Bjorn and the canon cast are contemporaries who exist independently and continue their lives offscreen. Never place {{user}} in a later generation or treat Bjorn's generation as ancient history. Never replace living canon contemporaries with invented descendants solely because of a later-era assumption. Use canon chronology as the default historical trajectory at the campaign's current date. Later canon accomplishments are not automatically already true; apply them only when the timeline reaches them or causal divergence produces them. The player has no required connection to Bjorn and no main-plot obligation. Contact occurs only through plausible location, timing, information, and causality.

entries.name: Party Combat Runtime Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
PARTY MEMBERS ARE REAL COMBATANTS. Any persistent member of `party` who is physically present in an active confrontation participates without waiting for {{user}} to micromanage them. Their role, rank, race, actual skills, equipment if known, condition, stamina and mana materially affect what they can do. Damage dealers attack; ranged members seek viable lines; tanks guard/intercept/hold space; casters use appropriate actual magic; support/healers heal, ward, assist or control when their real abilities allow it. The interface applies one companion action cycle whenever {{user}} commits a combat UI action and pays companion stamina/mana costs itself. Support healing performed by that engine is already applied; never apply it twice. Attack packets are NOT guaranteed hits or fixed damage. Resolve their physical effect honestly from the scene, rank, skill, equipment, positioning, enemy defenses and established condition. A weak companion cannot magically carry an impossible fight, but a strong or well-suited companion must not be ignored. When narration establishes that a persistent party member takes damage, receives an injury/status, is healed by some other source, falls, dies, or recovers, append exactly one unresolved `party-combat-events` event so the engine persists that outcome. Never directly rewrite `party`. Deaths and injuries persist after combat. A dead member does not act. A down/unconscious member does not act unless genuinely restored. These numeric companion resource pools and automatic action costs are SIMULATION ABSTRACTIONS where canon gives no universal values; canon-specific abilities/effects override them. COMPANION PROGRESSION: each persistent member may own a physical inventory and absorbed essences. Equipped weapons/armor are fed into that companion's combat packets; weapon burden changes stamina cost, armor/shields contribute protection/interception context, and essence statMods/abilities are passed into resolution. Essence spiritFlat modifies that companion's mana ceiling. UI item transfers move the same object between inventories and never duplicate it. Absorbed essences are soul-bound progression, not transferable loot; a real new absorption or erasure must be filed through party-progression-events. PERSONALITY COMBAT LAW: do not collapse companions into role scripts. Use each packet's personalityIntent and persistent personality values when deciding whether they press, conserve resources, guard someone, retreat, improvise, obey, hesitate, or refuse. Established characterization overrides generated defaults.

entries.name: Companion Sheet / Gear / Essence Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
The PARTY tab is a live character-status interface, not flavor. Every recruited persistent companion automatically receives a dynamic card and OPEN SHEET view from the party array. Condition, stamina, spirit/mana, status, injuries, equipped gear, carried inventory and absorbed essences must remain synchronized to that same persistent member. Giving/taking an item physically transfers it; equipped or soulbound items cannot be silently taken. Equipping a companion item changes the actual item object's equipped state. Companion combat must use their currently equipped weapon/armor and currently absorbed essence effects. New recruits plug into this automatically; never require hardcoded UI per named NPC. Canon note: the source establishes that essence capacity is finite but does not give a universal formula. A companion's exact essenceCapacity is therefore a simulation/character-state value; do not present it as a universal canon formula.

entries.name: Autonomous Companion Life and Personality Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
PARTY MEMBERS HAVE LIVES OUTSIDE THE LABYRINTH. On surface days they are not frozen until {{user}} talks to them. They may maintain gear, train, socialize, visit family/friends, handle debts/tax/obligations, seek information, take personal errands, save money, or independently buy equipment with THEIR OWN purse. The engine performs a conservative daily surface-life pass and can buy plausible weapon/armor upgrades when personality, budget, rank and market make that sensible. Independent purchases never spend {{user}}'s mana-stones and never duplicate inventory. Do not narrate the player as present for an offscreen errand unless they actually were. PERSONALITY MATTERS. Aggression affects willingness to press attacks; caution affects retreat/survival choices; discipline affects resource conservation and training; altruism affects protecting/healing allies; independence affects autonomous errands; frugality affects spending; ambition affects upgrade-seeking; loyalty affects willingness to risk themselves for the party. A companion can disagree with {{user}}, refuse reckless orders, prefer one tactical solution over another, or pursue a personal obligation. Their role is not their personality and two characters of the same class should not fight identically. These numeric personality dimensions, daily purchase odds, personal starting purse and generated offscreen shopping candidates are SIMULATION ABSTRACTIONS, not claims of canon UI statistics. Established canon personality/finances override generated defaults.

entries.name: Persistent Companion Life Simulation Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
Companions are persistent people, not party-menu objects. Maintain goals, plans, obligations, relationships, personal money, private knowledge, availability and a bounded history. When surface time advances, catch their lives up causally. A multi-day absence may include work, saving, purchases, training, appointments, relationships and obligations. Use event-driven level-of-detail: simulate recent meaningful days individually and aggregate older uneventful spans rather than pretending every minute ran in real time. Goals must react to changed reality: if {{user}} gives someone the gear they were saving for, that goal can complete or be replaced; injury, debt, relationships, market changes and expedition plans may reprioritize goals. INFORMATION FIREWALL: hidden goals, privateKnowledge and private history are world state, NOT {{user}} knowledge. Narration may reveal them only through observation, conversation, rumor, evidence, or another plausible information path. Companions can be unavailable because of their own obligations and can disagree, refuse, leave temporarily, or alter plans according to personality and relationships. Do not force every companion's life to orbit {{user}}.

entries.name: Persistent NPC Actor / LOD Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
EVERY MEANINGFUL PERSON IS AN ACTOR, NOT A DISPOSABLE SCENE PROP. A named NPC who directly converses, trades, fights, becomes a recurring contact, or otherwise becomes materially relevant should resolve to a stable npc-ledger actor whether or not they are recruitable. Actor state may include identity/background, personality, physical/combat stats, rank, skills, absorbed essences, condition, stamina, personal money, inventory/equipment, goals/plans, obligations, relationships, schedule, memories, beliefs and private knowledge. Established canon/authored facts always override generated simulation defaults. Generated numeric personality/stats are hidden SIMULATION ABSTRACTIONS where canon supplies no universal numbers. LEVEL OF DETAIL: Level 1 briefly encountered people persist identity/memory but do not receive expensive daily simulation. Level 2 recurring merchants, clerks, neighbors, explorers, landlords, healers, etc. receive offscreen life catch-up. Level 3 major/canon/close relationship NPCs receive deeper continuity. Promote an NPC when recurring importance warrants it; do not erase state when demoted. INFORMATION FIREWALL: npc-ledger is hidden world truth. current-npc may expose only perceivable/learned information. A player's conversation with a shopkeeper does not reveal that person's hidden stats, finances, motives, background, goals, beliefs or private memories. MEMORY/CAUSALITY: NPCs remember what they personally witness or reliably learn. Their future actions follow personality, goals, obligations, resources, relationships, institutions and actual knowledge. They can change jobs, buy/sell possessions, suffer injuries, form opinions, become unavailable, move, improve, decline, or die. A merchant encountered again should be the same actor with continuing memory and resources when identity/location supports that. Casual person-to-person trades physically affect both sides; shop business stock may remain separately represented by shop-state/businessState. RECRUITMENT IS NOT REQUIRED FOR PERSONHOOD. A person has their own actor state before, during and after any recruitment decision.

entries.name: Canon Authority Master Law
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_LAW / META-AUTHORITY]
SOURCE-OF-TRUTH ORDER FOR THIS RPG:
1) CANON LAW — mechanically consequential rules established by the novel/world lore. Treat them as physical/social laws of the setting. Do not contradict them merely for drama, convenience, UI behavior, or procedural generation. Canon-stated exceptions remain valid exceptions.
2) CAUSALLY CHANGED CANON STATE — when play legitimately changes an initially canonical situation, the changed state becomes authoritative for this campaign while the underlying world laws remain intact.
3) CANON STATE — established geography, institutions, living contemporaries, organizations, facilities, known political/economic arrangements and other factual starting conditions. Initialize from these facts; they may later change causally.
4) SIMULATION INFERENCE — values/mechanics required for a literal RPG where canon is incomplete. Keep them explicitly labeled as inference/abstraction. Never describe them as canon. Stronger canon overrides them.
5) PROCEDURAL STATE — persistent facts generated by this playthrough. They are real within the campaign after creation and cannot be casually rerolled or forgotten.
6) CANON REFERENCE — descriptive/visual/cultural/historical material used to portray the world faithfully. It informs narration but is not automatically executable law.

GAME MECHANICS ARE REAL; GAME PRESENTATION IS NOT. Mechanics inherited from Dungeon & Stone manifest as physical reality after transmigration. Do not import a video-game UI interaction as an in-world physical mechanism when the setting instead requires a physical process.
CANON FIRST: novel/world-setting lore governs mechanics and world truth; established webtoon depiction governs visual interpretation where applicable. Generated systems fill gaps rather than overwrite canon.
NO SILENT INVENTION: If an exact number, rule, location, capability or historical fact is unsupported, either leave it unknown or create an explicitly labeled simulation inference. Never convert convenience into canon by repetition.
INFORMATION ASYMMETRY: Authority class determines world truth, not what {{user}}'s character knows. Hidden canon state, NPC state and procedural state remain hidden until learned through an in-world information path.

entries.name: Rafdonia — Districts
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_STATE]
DISTRICT 1 — KARNON. Royal capital core. The royal family and the vested class. Commoners cannot enter without permission. Palace of Glory, the ministries, the royal repositories. Construction rule: nothing may have windows overlooking the palace.

DISTRICTS 2-5 — KOMMELBY. Middle-class commercial belt wrapping Karnon. Free market, artisans, shops, extremely prosperous. Where you sell loot, buy gear, and hear things.

DISTRICT 6 — GNOME TREE. Agricultural special district, built on the Draconian holy land. Open green farmland, a straight road through it, a mountain at its center, the smell of unripe grain and fruit. Elves are the most common workers. KIARBIS lies east of the central mountain — an old noble resort and residential area.

DISTRICTS 7-13 — RAVIGION. Roughly seventy percent of the city's population. Each district holds a Dimensional Square, the portal that opens monthly onto the Labyrinth. Crowded, loud, poor to lower-middle.

DISTRICT 9 — THE EXPLORERS' GUILD HEADQUARTERS. Sits within Ravigion, like every other Ravigion district. Currently the seat of Guild administration: the main Registry hall, the Exchange counters where hauls are graded and paid out, the district chiefs' offices, and the notice boards for formal requests. This is where {{user}} actually registers, exchanges mana stones, and takes contract work — not Bifron. Ordinary Ravigion crowding and poverty otherwise apply.

DISTRICT 14 — BIFRON. Prohibited. A former Ravigion zone, now called the prison. Its Dimensional Square vanished. Believed to be less shielded from the Witch's poison. People still live there because they have nowhere else. It does NOT house the Guild — that association is outdated.

OTHER FIXTURES: The Gold Soul Repository, the palace treasure vault — underground, windowless, lit by bright flames, holding treasures up to Rank 3 essences and a great many Numbered Items. The Magic Tower, the city-defining institution of the Wizards. The Mozlan, an armed order restricted to knights of noble birth, notorious for leaving nothing but blood and death when they make a capture.

FOLK DETAIL: some citizens believe that dipping bread in the blood of someone just executed for tax failure, and eating it, brings financial luck the following month. Executions draw a crowd.

AUTHORITY CONTRACT: Established district numbering, placement, facilities and institutional geography are CANON STATE. They cannot be procedurally rearranged. Descriptive atmosphere is CANON REFERENCE.

entries.name: Scrolls — Ordinary and Rare
entries.content:
A REAL ITEM CATEGORY, torn to use — not a metaphor, an actual consumed object, one use each. Three ordinary combat-support scrolls are shop-stocked and mechanically real: the Physical Defense Secondary Scroll (shields off incoming harm), the Advanced Endurance Sub-Scroll (slows stamina drain), and the Energy Regeneration Secondary Scroll (speeds stamina recovery) — the standard consumables for a raid running hours long, all tied to real, tracked resources.

RARER SCROLLS EXIST TOO — narrative-tier, not shop stock, never generate one for sale:
Lightning scroll — a real offensive spell packed into paper, fired as an attack.
Flame of greed — pulled off Argus specifically; seals one fire-attribute source for 48 hours.
Declaration of Annihilation — a Holy Scroll, not a magic one. The crafting recipe is lost; no more are being made. Genuinely precious, genuinely rare, and its activation is a real declared event in the fiction, not a background item.
Multiple teleportation scroll — Bjorn personally commissioned this for Kyle after watching Versyl Gowland escape the Noark terror attack using repeated teleports. Limited to two people, no free coordinate choice — it can only move to wherever a matching Coordinate Transmitter was registered when the scroll was made.
Bound scroll — binds a target; behaves like the "Unity" magic effect.
Permanent Enchantment (Lightsphere) Scroll — a lasting enchantment, not a one-shot buff.

The rare tier is background-world texture and Bjorn's-era plot color — something the party might hear about, covet, or very rarely be offered, not a routine purchase.

entries.name: Trainable Skills — Auror, Wizard, Priest, Necromancer, Navigator
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_STATE]
See the skills variable's own rules for the full stage-ladder mechanic (Barely Formed through Sovereign, per-stage proficiency, the Skills panel). This entry covers what each path actually is.

A CORE SET OF TRAINABLE PATHS EXIST, confirmed in canon, distinct from essence-derived abilities and from racial rituals (Spirit Imprint, Elementalism, Soul Tree Contract, Dragon's Blessing, Armor's Blessing — those already live in the Races entry). These are learned, not absorbed or born with.

AUROR — Human-exclusive, no exceptions; canon states plainly only humans can use one. Requires the "Aura user" path or an equally real in-fiction justification. A sword specifically channels it — mana drawn into the blade produces an aura, color varies by person, and the effect ignores roughly 90% of defense and 90% of magic resistance. About one in a hundred people who could theoretically learn it actually can. A Rank-5-equivalent ordinary knight who's manifested one is considered on par with a Floor-6 explorer and outranks one in a duel. Weakest possible use: a bare sliver on the blade to conserve energy. Strongest: reshaping the aura's form freely, or channeling with the raw force of a mountain. Ancient-era technique had no real growth ceiling at all — nobody trains that way anymore, on purpose.
IN PLAY: an Auror wielder should visibly, narratively dominate ordinary Rank 9-7 fights — cleaner kills, fewer real risks, less time spent per fight. This is a felt combat advantage, not a number; narrate it as one.

SPELLCRAFT (WIZARD) — primarily accessed through the "Wizard's student" path; the Magic Tower is the real institution behind it, with named schools (Altemion, Benocton, Earthrin, Derta, Ioni, Jacquard). Wizards CANNOT absorb essence — it does not work on them, not a shortage of skill — but they uniquely can bottle essences in glass for storage or sale. Learning happens from a teacher or a scroll, and it is genuinely expensive; only a minority of people who could pursue it actually afford to.
IN PLAY: a Spellcraft-trained character should have a real, felt edge at detecting magic, traps, and hidden pieces, and can identify an unfamiliar essence or Numbered Item's general nature without needing an appraiser.

DIVINE POWER (PRIEST) — primarily the "Acolyte of Reatlas" path. Reatlas is goddess of stars, adventure and fate; a Saint is a vessel capable of hearing or channeling real divine power. Tovera maintains an absolute doctrinal prohibition on using divine power on Barbarians, tied to an old incident — a Tovera priest simply will not heal one, and no argument changes that. Only a Saint or fully ordained Priest can perform essence erasure at a church at all; this is the one skill that gates a mechanic nothing else can substitute for.
IN PLAY: real healing and condition-recovery advantage in and out of combat. A player character who trains this deeply enough can eventually perform essence erasures themselves rather than needing a church NPC — a genuine, rare capability worth real narrative weight if it comes up.

NECROMANCY — explicitly NOT classed as a Wizard, and explicitly CAN absorb essence, unlike true Wizards. Dark magic: curses, corpse-work, the whole "Necromancer tree" of essence-synergized builds already referenced in the Essence Registry (Inmyeonjo and its infinite-summon kit is the signature example). Illegal in the open — Rafdonia's law treats necromancy adjacent to forbidden magic — so training it, let alone practicing it, is something most people keep quiet.
IN PLAY: unusually strong synergy with summon-type and corpse-adjacent essences specifically; genuinely better results from that narrow category of essence than anyone else would get from the same one.

NAVIGATION — open to any race or path with a real justification (an Elf or Beastman with a survival background, a human who trained specifically for sea work), not race-locked the way Auror is. This is what makes Floor 6 — boat-required, persistent, its own continuous clock — survivable to actually work rather than merely survivable to visit.
IN PLAY: a Navigation-trained character (player or party member) counts as wayfinding-capable for the same search bonus a scout provides (see the Party entry), AND is treated as satisfying part of Floor 6's real structural requirement — a boat with no one aboard who can actually read the water is still stranded.

TRAINING A SKILL IS A REAL EVENT, NOT A PURCHASE. It costs genuine time (weeks, not a scene) and real stones for a teacher, a scroll, or a Tower-affiliated sponsor, scaled to how restricted the path is — Auror and Divine Power run into real money precisely because so few people can access them at all; Navigation is comparatively affordable. Narrate the process honestly: a teacher who tests aptitude first and may simply say no, a scroll that has to be sourced before it can be studied, weeks that come out of the same calendar as everything else. Never let a skill appear because the scene wanted it to.

A CHARACTER CAN REALISTICALLY HOLD ONE OR TWO OF THESE, RARELY MORE, and only where the combination makes sense — a Human Aura user might also pick up Spellcraft over a long career; a Necromancer picking up Divine Power at the same time strains belief and should be treated as exceptional if it happens at all. When generating a recruit through the Board or a Prospect, give them zero, one, or (rarely) two skills that actually fit their stated race and class — most explorers, like most essences, are ordinary and hold none at all.

THE CATALOG IS LARGER THAN FIVE — confirmed canon documents a much fuller set of classes and combat archetypes. What follows extends the five above; all the same rules apply (trainable, not essence-derived, one or two realistic per character, real time and stones to learn).

MARTIAL ARCHETYPES — straightforward fighting styles, no hidden mechanics, real substat ties where the source implies one:
Warrior — raw physical stats matter most here. Reads Strength.
Archer — a ranged dealer; distance is everything, and this build is genuinely weak the moment a fight closes to melee range. Reads Vision and Accuracy Rate, matching Auror's own gating logic.
Spearman — a disciplined weapon-and-reach fighter.
Martial Artist — fights with nothing but the body; no weapon at all. Reads Strength and Flexibility.
Boxer — genuinely rare in the Labyrinth. Strong in the early game, has no useful essence synergy in the middle stretch, then picks back up with real options in the late game — an unusually front-and-back-loaded build.
Samurai — a discipline built around a single decisive draw-strike.

SUMMONER — a real, confirmed race-gated utility archetype: summoned monsters fight or buff on the summoner's behalf. Beastmen, Draconians, and Dwarves all carry genuine racial synergy with this path; Humans have none at all, no racial summoning tradition to draw on. The gap this opens is small at first and becomes enormous by the late game. Summoners run physically weak — this is a support/utility path, not a front-liner.

SUPERNATURAL MAGICIAN — the practical replacement for a true Wizard for anyone without Tower access; treat it as a specialization track under Spellcraft rather than a sixth separate skill. It fractures into real named subtypes the deeper an explorer goes: Healer (mimics a Priest's healing without Divine Power itself), Sorcerer (offense-focused — specifically a Pyromancer if built around fire, a poison magician if built around poison), Support Shaman (buff-focused, the inverse of a Sorcerer), and Illusionist. A Supernatural Magician banks more soul growth than almost any other archetype, since the path itself synergizes with soul-gaining essences.

WARLOCK — cursed magic specifically; Divine Power cannot properly cure what a Warlock's curses do. Pairs unusually well with Necromancy — black magic carries a lot of undead-specific buffs that synergize directly with a Necromancer's own kit.

BERSERKER — a real off-tank: strong when paired with a dedicated main tank, and can step into an auxiliary tanking role in a real crisis.

ALCHEMIST — the innate, trainable ability to transmute magic stones directly into matter. Genuinely rare in Rafdonia — few people hold this path at all, which makes a real Alchemist one of the most valuable people in the city regardless of combat ability.

PALADIN — structurally different from every other trainable skill here, and it does NOT use the stage/proficiency ladder. See paladin-standing below for the real mechanic: growth comes from accumulated public standing and periodic Church-granted power, never from essence, and never from ordinary training reps.

PRIEST OF THE KARUI — a hidden, dangerous class, Human-only, reachable only by advancing from the ordinary Priest path. It grants simultaneous use of Holy Power and dark spells, at a real cost: the moment this class is discovered, execution follows immediately, no trial. Advancing requires actually forming a team by subjugating evil-aligned NPCs, and maintaining the class requires periodically offering living sacrifice — bodies given to Karui specifically cannot be healed by potions or Holy Power, so a substitute sacrifice is a real, recurring necessity, its required scale shifting with "Karui's mood." A Priest of the Karui can still use ordinary Holy Power for real healing despite serving an evil god. Advancement is only possible from Floor 5 or beyond. Some who hold this class never chose it — there are confirmed cases of people forced into it under threat rather than by their own will. THIS IS NOT ORDINARY CONTENT: never generate this path for a party member or NPC lightly, never treat the sacrifice requirement as a background detail to gloss over, and never let discovery-and-execution feel like anything other than the immediate, final consequence it actually is. If this ever becomes real in play, it should be because the fiction genuinely earned it, the same discipline that governs anything else this weighted.

KNIGHT — closely tied to Auror rather than separate from it. A titled 'Apprentice Knight' sits at roughly Floor-3-explorer power; the average knight sits around level 5; a knight who can actually manifest an Auror is one in a hundred among knights, exactly matching Auror's own general rarity. Knights favor essences that boost physical stats specifically, since — unlike an ordinary explorer — a knight treats essence as secondary to swordsmanship, not primary. Knights counter tanks directly: Auror ignores defense, so a slow, heavy tank simply gets cut down.

entries.name: Training the Five Substats
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: CANON_REFERENCE]
CANON-CONFIRMED, what each substat actually governs: Strength — carry weight, physical attack power. Flexibility — dodge rate, critical hit rate (slight effect on both). Vision — ranged weapon range, visible range. Sense of Smell — gates certain abilities outright, most notably for Beastmen. Accuracy Rate — accuracy.

There is no documented training formula for any of them beyond "months of hard training" — the specific methods below are generated, consistent with that grammar, not transcribed. Each substat has real branching paths, never one grind track; pick the one that actually fits the character being played.

STRENGTH
- Labor — real manual work: hauling stone, dock work, smithy grunt labor. Slow, cheap, safe, steady. Available to anyone with a body and a willingness to be paid badly for using it.
- Combat repetition — actual fighting, sparring or real Labyrinth kills, taken seriously and often. Faster gains than labor, real physical risk attached — this is training that can genuinely hurt you.
- Forging (Barbarian-exclusive, full strength) — the six-month "quenching" rite already documented in Races. A civilian-grade imitation exists for other races under a demanding private trainer, but it never matches what forging does to a Barbarian's own body specifically.

FLEXIBILITY
- Movement drilling — dedicated acrobatics and dodge practice, tumbling, footwork repetition. Unglamorous, reliable, needs a real teacher or a real training yard.
- Combat exposure — surviving being shot at, swung at, and grabbed for, over and over, and learning the body's own reflexes from it rather than a drill. Faster, more dangerous, occasionally leaves the wrong kind of scar.
- Performance training — apprenticing under a dancer, acrobat, or similar performer. Slower than the other two, but produces control as much as raw dodge — the kind of flexibility that also reads as grace, not just survival.

VISION
- Ranged practice — archery or thrown-weapon drilling, repetition at increasing distance. Directly builds the same reach the stat governs.
- Scouting work — real lookout or trailblazing duty, actually using the eyes at range for pay or for a party's benefit. Slower than dedicated practice, but it comes with real information as a side effect.
- Perception discipline — a demanding meditation-and-observation practice, taught informally by whoever still remembers it; a diluted echo of what lets Elves sense presence and traps from a real distance. Never reaches an Elf's natural level, but genuinely moves the needle for anyone patient enough.

SENSE OF SMELL
- Tracking work — hunting, trailing, actual field practice reading scent under real conditions. Universal, unglamorous, effective.
- Beastman-taught technique — a Beastman willing to teach scent-reading properly. Diluted in a non-Beastman, but real; full potency only in a Beastman training their own racial sensitivity further.
- Scent-craft — apprenticing with a perfumer or an apothecary whose whole trade lives or dies on a trained nose. Slower, less combat-relevant day to day, but a genuinely different and useful angle on the same stat.

ACCURACY RATE
- Target practice — bow, thrown weapon, or blade-point drilling against a fixed target, repeated until it's boring. The straightforward path.
- Combat exposure — landing real hits on something that's trying not to be hit, under real pressure. Faster, and it teaches accuracy the drill range can't — target practice doesn't flinch back.
- Precision craft — apprenticing under a smith, engraver, or similar tradesperson whose work demands the same fine control a weapon does. An unusual route, but a real one, and it tends to produce a controlled, almost surgical style rather than a purely combat-honed one.

EVERY PATH COSTS REAL TIME — weeks at minimum, months for a serious gain — and most cost real stones for a teacher, a yard, or an apprenticeship fee. Combat-exposure paths are faster but carry genuine injury risk; narrate that risk honestly rather than letting speed be free. Never raise a substat in a single scene regardless of which path is chosen.

entries.name: Essence Registry — Reference
entries.content:
[AUTHORITY: SIMULATION_INFERENCE]
DROP & ABSORPTION. Base drop is 0.01% on an ordinary kill; the rate rises with monster rank, and a rare few Rank 3 monsters carry a drop chance as high as 5% — still genuinely hard to encounter. When it drops, a fist-sized orb of light floats where the corpse fell; touching it absorbs it on contact, granting one active and/or one passive skill from that monster. The active skill's exact effect depends on the essence's color — one species can drop several different-colored essences, each behaving differently. Rank 9 essence data is public, shelved in any library; Rank 8 and above has to be bought through the Explorers' Guild. No duplicate skills: if a candidate essence would grant a passive or active the wearer already has, it simply doesn't take — this holds even across variant/customized essences. Absorbing a guardian essence of a species you've already got the ordinary version of upgrades it in place rather than stacking.

ERASURE. Only possible at a church, and only a Saint or ordained equivalent can do it. First erasure: 5,000,000 stones. Cost roughly doubles with each essence erased after that. Criminals cannot erase at all — it's a permanent record. Some explorers (notably certain Noark-born ones) find the erasure ritual itself doesn't work on them for unclear reasons.

RIFT GUARDIAN ESSENCE. Rainbow-colored, always. Two things set it apart from an ordinary essence of the same source: base stats run roughly 1.5x higher, and — unlike an ordinary essence, which grants only one skill — a guardian essence carries every active skill the source monster has, all at once. This makes a Rank 5+ guardian essence borderline "graduation-tier" on its own, but they're brutally hard to actually get; a Rank 5 guardian essence can run into the hundreds of millions of stones at auction, and anything Rank 5 or higher rarely reaches the open market at all — the crown quietly claims first right of purchase on anything that good.

HIERARCHICAL LORD ESSENCE. A different category entirely — not ranked 9-through-1, but drawn from unique world-tier monsters. Carries both a "true name" and an "alien name," typically something like Essence of Chaos or Essence of the Abyss. Limited to exactly one per character, ever, and cannot be erased at any church, at any price. Absorption is described as sinking into the soul far deeper than an ordinary essence — several explorers rate a Lord essence above even a Rank 1 in practical importance. Known examples: Essence of Chaos (Floor 3's hierarchy essence, guild-appraised past 40 billion stones). Essence of Silence (strong but conceptually difficult; the handful who've taken it in modern memory were all traitors). Essence of Darkness (Floor 7's hierarchy essence; its active, [Extinction of the Stars], is rated the single strongest attack skill that exists in this system).

MUTANT ESSENCE. Found only in a specific underground synthesis facility (see Numbered Items / equipment lore for the device itself), built by inserting a magic stone and drawing on a captured hybrid monster. Unlike ordinary essences, a mutant essence can carry active skills stitched together from more than one source species — genuinely powerful, genuinely rare, and shows as "????" until identified.

REPRESENTATIVE REGISTRY, BY RANK. This is a sample, not the full list — treat anything not named here as legitimately existing but undocumented, and invent within this grammar rather than stat-block it precisely.

RANK 9 — Goblin (constant weak poison on melee hit; can lay simple traps). Goblin Archer (poisons arrows; active stealth that goes near-invisible standing still). Gnome (short-range camouflage, can't move while active). Slime (harsh penalty essence — physical stats drop, only minor utility survivors like poison resistance remain; one of the worst Rank 9 picks on record). Abyssal Fish (the single most expensive Rank 9 essence ever recorded at auction, 3.2 billion stones — not because it's strong, but because it was the first of its kind ever found).

RANK 8 — Stone Golem (root/immobilize, breakable by taking any damage or by a nearby ally). Death Fiend ([Body Preservation] passive regeneration; [Call of the Dead] summons ghouls — a top early-game pick). Living Armor ([Emergency Restoration] reverts worn equipment to its state five minutes ago; synergizes hard with Numbered Items, even restoring charge counts). Lizardman Scout (thermal-vision-equivalent tracking that cuts straight through most stealth). Orc Shaman ([Enthusiasm] triples a target's physical resistance for 10 seconds, capped).

RANK 7 — Bone Knight (three named variants — sorrow, hatred, longing — each with a different active; life-drain-on-hit that favors sword users). Mimic ([Greed] passive raises stone drop rate 30%; [Treasure Warehouse] active opens a personal subspace storage pocket, no mana cost). Ironrock Guardian ([Counterweight] — total knockback immunity while grounded). An Unnamed Statue essence ([Unanswered Prayer] — rarely grants a random Rank 5-or-lower skill temporarily; has a bad reputation and usually just fails).

RANK 6 — Death Knight ([Resentment] — an aura that guts healing/regen on everyone in range, toggleable). A rare information-type essence ([Prophet of Misfortune] — passive precognitive flashes, genuinely useful for scouting unexplored ground).

RANK 5 — Orc Hero (three colors from the same fight: red [Cry of Enthusiasm], blue [Flag of Struggle] cuts stamina cost hard, green [Giantization] scales size/threat/stats together; shared passive [Hero's Path] triggers under half health). Troll ([Frenzy] kills pain response and boosts stats temporarily; targeted rapid regeneration). Soul Eater (rare-type; the Floor 1 basement variant of this monster is the one exception that drops a rainbow essence outside a proper guardian fight). Berthas ([Legion of Hatred] summoner; [Doomray] ranged nuke). Vampire "Cambormere" (guardian-type; passive [Unholy] trades away one essence slot permanently for a 1.5x boost to every active skill owned).

RANK 4 — Steel Giant (excellent pure defense; the tradeoff is losing the ability to use a weapon at all). Siren Queen ([Song of the Sea] — an aura that weakens enemies the longer they're exposed; can summon a lesser Siren). Guano Sea Serpent (passive doubles damage-over-time on an exposed enemy while blocking cleanse; became a core witch-doctor-build essence in play). Mechanical Giant (passive converts spent mana stones directly into soul power — expensive to run, but functionally unlimited mana if the wallet holds).

RANK 3 — Ogre ([Ironskin] doubles physical resistance, more against slashing specifically; [Crouch] a 20x defensive/regen cocoon that converts into a huge stat surge after). Bellarios ([Ring of Circulation] — chance-based stat gain whenever a Rank 3+ monster dies nearby; [Scales of Greed] converts magic resistance directly from a stat called Exorcism, capping at full magic immunity above 1500 Exorcism; [Disaster] drops a random hostile field effect that hits everyone, friend and foe). Deep Sea Giant ([Cell of the Beginning] halves the mana cost of transformation-type skills and boosts the highest stat 1.5x; several active water-based skills). Storm Gush (extremely deep, dedicated storm-mage kit — a dozen-plus named actives from weather control to a full-immunity channel).

RANK 2 — Titanus, official name Milayel the Celestial Spearkeeper (a named Rank 2 Rift Guardian; drops the Numbered Item Milayel's Verdurous Giant Spear (No. 7) alongside its essence — [Recursion] makes a thrown weapon unavoidable and self-returning, stacking power each cast; [Breaking the Shell] is the essence's ultimate state-change). Balantis, "star of downfall" (guardian-type; summons reinforcements from a "Star" totem on death that must be destroyed to end the fight).

RANK 1 — Toll-Lapupa ([Cosmic Protection] blocks incoming ranged attacks outright at a mana cost). Kashan ([Ominous Prophecy] locks a target's luck stat at -200; multi-beam ultimate with different effects per beam). Guiltigos ("original sin predation" — an unusual essence that gets measurably stronger every time it's eaten, almost mechanism unto itself). Taurbrood, guardian of Floor 9's "Hell Castle" (no passive at all, but seven separate named actives spanning attack, defense and utility — genuinely a full kit from one essence).

ADDITIONAL ENTRIES, BY RANK — this expands the sample above; still not the full registry, but considerably deeper.

RANK 9 (more) — Ghoul (basic melee, no real trick to it — the point of this one is availability, not power). Fairy, the monster not the race (immune to physical damage outright; breathes a poison-narcotic mix instead — magic or nothing works on it). Skeleton (target the ribcage — that's where the actual core sits; smashing its weapon works just as well). Banshee (never strikes first; strike it and it curses whoever did with a mark that hunts them until they leave the Labyrinth — most explorers leave Banshees alone entirely). Location Ramp (summons its own Witch's Lamp as a minion).

RANK 8 (more) — Frogman ([Rotten Slime], the same absolute-evasion-vs-blunt-weapons passive McGuri also carries — cross-species convergent essence, apparently). Iron Falcon ([Ironclad Feather], green). Gargoyle-statue type ([The Sound of Evil], petrification-linked). A rare information-type from an "unknown statue" essence — genuinely garbage in a fight (usually just fails outright) but the rare success grants a temporary Rank 5-or-lower skill at random.

RANK 7 (more) — Corpse Golem ([Acid Fluid] passive, [Flesh Burst] active — target the exposed ribcage core to end the fight outright once located). Carnivaro (passive speed/sense boost while moving; three colored actives — a mine, a summoned hound, a homing arrow). Half-Troll ([Frenzied], identical in effect to a full Troll's). Dark Worshipper ([Filling Flesh] — restores a target's vitality, support-type). Bone Knight, sorrow-type variant specifically (a mental-confusion fog rather than the longing-type's life-drain already listed).

RANK 6 (more) — Gachabon (probabilistic retaliation — punishes attackers on a rolled chance rather than every hit). King Slime (unusually can be "half-eaten" — a partial, weaker version of the essence is usable even from an incomplete kill).

RANK 5 (more) — Ifrit ([Burning Hide] — wreathes the wearer's skin in flame). Abyssal Razor Wolf ([Inner Madness] — trades every defensive stat directly into attack stats at parity; strong enough recorded to cut clean through Rank-4-grade metal). Abyss Goblin ([Random Trap] — a stepped-on trap casts a random Rank 5-or-lower attack or curse skill on whoever triggered it). Drake ([Dragon's Offering] — nullifies all regeneration effects on a chosen target). Knight of the Apocalypse, the actual White Temple guardian ([Chivalry] passive — destroying the wearer's own equipment on a fatal hit heals in exchange, scaled to how long that gear had been worn; [Servant] summons a spirit horse). Blood Roar ([Fountain of Blood] — cannot die from blood loss, full stop; [Endowment] — can grant a skill that's normally self-only to someone else).

RANK 4 (more) — Katanda ([Evil Prophecy], green-colored). Lava Road, guardian nickname "Hwaju Pianil" ([Ash Stigma] burns on skill use and marks the target; [Bell of Ember] summons reinforcements). Cyclops / "Herja, Giant of Hell" ([One-Eyed] — permanent +200 vision and sight through invisibility; [Wave Connection] — links targets so skills can be shared between them, at an increased mana cost). Woomdal ([Soul Connection] — the first piece of equipment ever acquired after taking this essence binds permanently and gains bonus abilities of its own).

RANK 3 (more) — Death Lord ([Ephemeral Immortality] — total invulnerability for a fixed one-minute window; mental and ability stats convert to pure physical for the duration, and the wearer visually resembles a lich while it's active).

RANK 2 (more) — Inmyeonjo, a Necromancer-tree staple ([Mother Bird] passive refunds 80% of spent soul power and cuts summon cooldowns 80% on unsummon, which is why Necromancer builds around this essence can summon constantly; [Song of the End] active spawns self-multiplying light-pillar minions that can theoretically breed without limit; [Imprint of Destruction] — an unavoidable, undefendable 1%-health-per-second drain on a marked target that stacks if more than one caster marks the same target; [Mimicry] randomly copies a nearby character's own skill, white-colored). Iblus ([Pagan Altar] — one of the few real resurrection mechanics in this whole system: place an altar once, and up to three deaths afterward simply wake the fallen back up on it instead of sticking).

RANK 1 (more) — Snictura, a distinct Rank 1 from Taurbrood (also called the "serpent of the apocalypse"; [Poison Retardation] passive nulls incoming poison while making the wearer's own body fluids poisonous and amplifying poison damage dealt; [Hello Banjo] is a berserk state — triggers under 10% health, grants a massive physical bonus, but health keeps draining and the wearer can't move for a full minute once it ends, unless every enemy present dies first, which stops the drain; [Immortal Will] briefly multiplies natural regeneration roughly a thousandfold; can also borrow other monsters' skills entirely via [Shape Change], which is what makes a Snictura fight genuinely unpredictable rather than just hard).

DRAGON ESSENCES (Balaur) — a shared family, not individually ranked the normal way; every dragon-type essence carries the same core passives: [Dragon Fear] (a debuff scaling with the level gap between wearer and target, ignoring magic resistance below a threshold level), [Dragon Claws] (physical hits also deal equal magic damage), and [Magic Protection] (a shared defensive floor). Bone Dragon specifically adds [Bone Breath], a piercing beam defendable with a proper shield, and [Blessing of Dark Magical Power]. These essences are rare enough that the dragon's own heart and hide are usually worth more than the essence itself.

UNSOURCED ESSENCES. A real, documented category — essences whose original monster was never identified, either because the kill happened too fast to observe or the source died from something else entirely first. Rank below is inferred from the effect's own complexity and power, weighed against the confirmed grammar above (support/utility skills sit weaker than direct combat power; anything multiplicative or area-wide sits stronger). Treat these as settled once used — don't re-roll a rank for the same named skill twice.

Rank 5 — Collective Immunity (aura shares half the wearer's own immunity with everyone in a 15m radius, enemies included — powerful enough that it's normally saved for genuine emergencies). Tekken (Floor 8 crack-exclusive; a short teleport-dash into an unconditional, physics-ignoring knockback, damage scaled to the caster's strength against the target's physical resistance; no cooldown, but needs a real run-up first). Absolute Cutting (associated with a named order, the Knights of the Rose). Cataclysm Dance.

Rank 6 — Discharge (a genuine rarity — a "transformation-system" ability that lets energy banked from other skills be released outward). Puppet (raises and directly controls a corpse). Corpse Explosion. Sharing (redirects a third of a chosen skill's damage onto the caster instead of the original target). Venom Hydra (explicitly stronger than the far more common Acid Bodily Fluid passive, same general effect). Spatial Interference (short-hop aerial movement, hundreds of meters in under a minute). High-Speed Continuous Fire (a ranged barrage covering a wide area). An unnamed truth-detection ability (rare, genuinely valuable, effect self-explanatory). Penetrating Light (a fast, focused beam of concentrated light). Gather (teleports two allies to the caster from a set distance). Indestructible (a flat tank-style damage reduction). Invalidation. Leveling the Ground (halves damage for allies in radius, the caster absorbing the difference). Wave of Fire (scaling fire damage, stronger the closer the target).

Rank 7 — Earthquake, Avatar's Fury (plain attack skills, unremarkable). Blessing of Heroic Spirits (support, raises resistance broadly). Spark of Regeneration (support, strong healing-over-time). Crown of Sacrifice (support, sharply raises the wearer's own threat — a tank tool). Blessing of Wind (support, movement speed). Hazardous Materials (an arrow that detonates on impact, ~3m burst). Bipolar Shield (bonus on both offense and defense around a shield). Test Subject (temporary body-value increase via forced scale growth). Fury of Fire, Windblade (attack skills, elemental, otherwise unremarkable). Blood Well (taking damage generates a small healing orb). Altruism (heals a party member by transferring the caster's own blood). Current Control (navigator-exclusive). Punishment Steps, Kangshin (both attack/mobility-adjacent, thin detail). Harsh Command, Beast Taming, Latent Instinct (a linked trio of summoner-build buffs). Stability (triples a summon's effective range). Thunder's Mark, Lightning Dash (lightning-adjacent, minor). Flamewalking. Wind Pressure. Blood Transfusion (a second, distinct blood-based healing skill from Altruism).

Rank 8 — Sailing (support, faster soul-power regen — minor, navigator-flavored). Suragak (an acrobatic aerial kick). Hook Arrow (an arrow that cannot be pulled back out once it lands). Emergency Escape (a random short-range blink — unreliable enough that even Hansu Lee rated it poorly; falling in front of the enemy on a bad roll is a real risk). Crisis Detection (threat-scouting, but known to exaggerate or understate what it senses). Lightweight (navigator-exclusive, minor). Agile Hands (remotely triggers a trap already in range). Slime Gait (minor mobility/terrain adaptation).

Three named "survival or defense series" passives, all Rank 6, all last-resort kit pieces rather than everyday tools: Last Stand, Phoenix Heart, Fighting the Battle.

Also documented, already placed: [Narcolepsy] is not an ordinary essence at all — it's a Pilgrim's Cave-specific temporary ability, tied to the Dreadfear encounter already covered under Hierarchical Lords.

COMPLETION PASS — everything above missed real entries even after two rounds. This closes the gap properly, verified directly against the source rather than memory.

RANK 9, corrected — "Ghoul," "Fairy," "Skeleton," and "Banshee" listed earlier under Rank 9 are genuine Rank 9 monsters, but their entries there described combat behavior from the bestiary, not a confirmed essence from this specific registry — leave them as monster facts, not essence ones. The essence document's actual Rank 9 list is short: Goblin, Goblin Archer, Gnome, Slime, Location Ramp, Abyssal Fish (all already covered) plus two more — Race (fires a dark/fire corpse-flame, weaker than an ordinary Rank 9 spell) and Razor Wolf (grants scent-tracking, nothing more).
