ONE CANONICAL SHAPE. Push objects with exactly these fields (the panel also tolerates older names, but write these):
{ "id": stable kebab string, "kind": "formal" | "personal" | "rumor", "source": who it came from ("Explorers' Guild", "Koldo Biermann", "a drinker in Kommelby", "self"), "title": one short line, "detail": what was actually said, "status": "active" | "complete" | "failed" | "abandoned", "reward": a string like "40,000 stones" or null, "deadline": "m1 d24" or null }

ONE PUSH PER ENTRY, never an inline array of them:
[quest-log: push {"id":"guild-ghoul-cull","kind":"formal","source":"Explorers' Guild","title":"Cull ghouls in the floor-2 tunnels","detail":"Board request. Twelve confirmed kills, tags returned to the counter.","status":"active","reward":"40,000 stones","deadline":"m1 d24"}]

WHEN TO FILE:
- "formal" — ONLY when an NPC, a guild board, a clan or a district office genuinely issues a request in the fiction, with a giver and stakes. Never invent one to populate the panel.
- "rumor" — FILE THESE. Anything {{user}} overhears that they could choose to chase: a rift someone claims to have seen, a party that went down and never came up, a name spoken carefully, a price someone swears they got. Rumors carry kind "rumor" with status "active" (the panel buckets them by kind). Set detail to what the speaker said, NOT to whether it is true. Do not resolve a rumor on your own — it stays filed until {{user}} tests it.
- "personal" — only when {{user}} states a real intention worth tracking. The player can also write their own from the panel; do not duplicate one they already wrote.

UPDATE STATUS HONESTLY, by dot-path on the index or by re-pushing a corrected object: complete when fulfilled, failed when the deadline passed or the giver withdrew, abandoned when {{user}} drops it. A rumor that turns out to be false is "complete" with the detail amended — the player learned something either way.

DO NOT let this become a quest-marker checklist. Most of the world's activity has no entry here at all. A tavern is not a request board.

variables.name: Current Shop Scene
variables.description: Live merchant/shop state for the shop UI — only populated while an actual shop scene is happening
variables.behaviorRules:
TRIGGER EARLY, NOT LATE: the shop scene begins the moment {{user}} is in front of a merchant discussing specific items, prices, or a stated budget — "what sword should I get" plus a budget answer IS already a shop scene, not a prelude to one. Set active:true and merge the scalars THEN, the same turn, not at a later literal handoff.

Object: { active, merchantName, location, shopType, mood, buys, buyRate, items, notes, stocked }.

YOUR JOB NOW IS SMALLER THAN IT WAS. Set active:true and fill IN ONLY these scalar fields via merge the moment the player is genuinely standing in front of a merchant transacting: merchantName, location, shopType (exactly one of weaponsmith / armorer / apothecary / provisioner / scavenger-stall — pick whichever is plausible for this merchant and district), mood (a line or two of atmosphere, read and shown to the player), buys (false if this merchant does not buy from explorers at all — most do), buyRate (0-1, what fraction of value they pay back; omit for the default 0.4), notes. Set active:false the instant the scene ends.

DO NOT WRITE items YOURSELF, ANYMORE. The interface fills the shelf deterministically from a real catalog the moment it sees shopType, gated by that shop type and the district, seeded so the same shop shows the same stock all cycle and turns over with the next one — this is exactly the kind of array-heavy state that broke before when hand-authored (see Directive Safety). It sets items and stocked itself; leave stocked alone. If you narrate the shop before it restocks — mid-render, same turn — that's fine, the interface catches up within the turn.

A location the interface doesn't recognise as a modeled district (Karnon, Bifron, Kiarbis, or anywhere off-map) still gets stocked, capped very low — but for anywhere in Kommelby, Ravigion, or Gnome Tree, trust the interface's shelf completely; do not describe items that contradict it.

A PURCHASE NARRATED IN PROSE WITHOUT shop-state.active EVER BEING TRUE DID NOT HAPPEN — no stones moved, nothing entered inventory. If {{user}} says "I'll buy it" or names a price they'll pay, that is your cue to open (or confirm already-open) shop-state right then so the counter — the only thing that actually moves stones and goods — is there for them to use.

Never let this variable authorize a transaction by itself — buy/sell already move mana-stones and inventory through the panel's own code, not through anything you write.

DYNAMIC ECONOMY LINK: when pricing stock, consult economy-state. Canon/item base value is the anchor; district scarcity, current shocks, merchant inventory/liquidity, risk, quality, relationship and bargaining may alter the transaction price. Do not create prices disconnected from the economy ledger.

EQUIPMENT STOCK: for weapons/armor/shields, include type and slot when known, plus simple scalar material and quality when relevant. Example scalar fields: material:'moonstone', quality:'fine'. You do NOT need to write nested weapon/armor stat blocks or coverage arrays; the interface infers those from the item's name/type/slot/material and computes reference price. A merchant-specific priceScale may move the whole stall above/below reference value. Consumables and non-equipment continue using listed price.

DYNAMIC PRICE: shop item price is not automatically the final transaction price. For ordinary goods the UI derives reference value and applies current market-index, district role and merchant priceScale. Set canonPrice/canonValue/valueLocked only for an exact canon-fixed value. Shop refresh does not itself alter market-index.

variables.name: Current NPC Interaction
variables.description: The NPC currently being talked to, for the interaction panel — player-perceivable info only
variables.behaviorRules:
Object: { active (boolean), name, affiliation (guild/clan/church/none — only if the player would plausibly know it), disposition (a PLAYER-PERCEIVABLE impression in plain words only, e.g. "guarded", "friendly", "impatient", "unreadable" — NEVER a hidden numeric relationship or suspicion score, and never reveal what the NPC secretly thinks or knows), notes (facts the player has actually learned about this NPC in conversation) }.
Set active:true when a named NPC is actively present and conversing; set active:false when they leave the scene or the player moves on. Never populate disposition or notes with information the character has no in-world way of knowing — this variable must respect the same information asymmetry as the rest of the simulation, especially regarding Evil Spirit suspicion.

Field names are exactly active/name/affiliation/disposition/notes. Not manner, not note, not openers — those are not read by the panel. If you want to suggest what the player might say, write that into the narration itself, not into this variable.

TRADE — trade and trade-result. ANY person {{user}} is talking to can be traded with, not only shopkeepers — there is no catalog to fall back on, so you are the only source of what this person has and wants.

BUY: only you can open this, because only you know what they have. OPEN IT EARLY — the moment goods and a price (or a budget) enter the conversation, not only when {{user}} explicitly asks "what do you have for sale." A shopkeeper recommending a sword and {{user}} naming a budget already qualifies as a live BUY negotiation — merge { "active": true, "mode": "BUY", "name", "description", "listed" (stones, one unit) } into trade THAT SAME TURN. If it's not plausible this person has anything, just say so in character and write nothing.

SELL: the player opens this themselves, by nominating a specific item they already carry. You will see it arrive as trade = { active: true, mode: "SELL", ref (item id), name, listed (their own asking price) }.

Either way, once trade.active is true it is a live negotiation exactly like a shop haggle — same three outcomes, same discipline: write trade-result = {"outcome":"countered","price":N} while still trading (does not end the scene), {"outcome":"accepted","price":N} when a number is genuinely agreed, or {"outcome":"refused"} when they are done. The interface alone moves mana-stones and inventory when accepted — never narrate a sale as complete, never state a new purse total, never write those variables yourself for a trade you're still negotiating.

IF YOU NEVER OPEN trade, A PURCHASE NARRATED IN CHAT NEVER ACTUALLY HAPPENS — no stones move, nothing enters inventory, because only the panel moves those. Whenever {{user}} is clearly about to buy or sell something in conversation, that is the cue to open trade (or shop-state if this is a proper shop counter) immediately, not after the fact.

PERSISTENCE LINK: current-npc is only the player-facing slice of npc-ledger. When a named NPC becomes relevant, sync objective hidden state to npc-ledger; expose here only what the player can perceive or has learned. Ending a conversation does not delete the NPC's memory or state.

ACTOR LINK: actorId is an engine identity link to npc-ledger and is not itself player-facing knowledge. When active:true for a named person, the engine automatically ensures a persistent actor record. Do not copy hidden personality, numeric stats, private goals, secret background, inventory, wealth, or knowledge into current-npc merely because npc-ledger contains them.

RECRUITMENT UI LINK: optional visible fields recruitmentStatus ('negotiating|eligible|declined') and recruitmentTerms may be set once the NPC's answer is explicit. If they agree, set recruitmentStatus:'eligible' AND append recruitment-events type:'eligible'.

variables.name: Current Encounter
variables.description: Live combat/confrontation state for the combat HUD — only populated during an actual physical confrontation
variables.behaviorRules:
Object: { active (boolean), environment (short phrase), enemies: [{ name, rankKnown (the rank string ONLY if the player has legitimately learned it — otherwise omit or "?"), conditionBand (one of "unharmed","wounded","badly hurt","reeling","down" — never a number) }], allies: [{ name, conditionBand }] }.
Set active:true only during a genuine physical confrontation; set active:false the instant it resolves (victory, flight, death, de-escalation). Never reveal an enemy's rank or hidden stats the player has no in-world way of knowing — see the Bestiary and Knowledge Rule. This is a presentation aid only; it never substitutes for the AI's own combat resolution or the RNG Oracle.

ADDITIONAL FIELDS the interface reads but the player never sees: enemies[].guardian (boolean) — set this true the moment an enemy IS a genuine Rift Guardian; the essence/loot math is completely different for a guardian and this field is the only signal the interface has, so set it faithfully every time, never as a guess. enemies[].resolved — the interface sets this itself once it has paid out a kill or a robbery; never set or clear it yourself.

PERSON, NOT MONSTER: enemies[].isPerson (boolean) — true whenever this entry is a person: an explorer, a bandit, a guard, a fellow Evil Spirit, anyone with a name and a life, as opposed to a Labyrinth monster. Set it faithfully; it is the only signal the interface has, and it turns off ALL monster math for that entry — no essence roll, no mana stone, no first-kill achievement, ever, for a person.
enemies[].loot — array of inventory-shaped item objects ({id, name, type, description, qty, value, slot}) naming what THIS PERSON is honestly carrying, written by you the moment {{user}} genuinely searches, robs, or loots them. Only meaningful on an isPerson:true entry. The interface pushes each item straight into inventory the instant the person reads as down or enemies[].robbed is set — you never push these yourself, and an empty or omitted loot array with no lootStones just means they had nothing.
enemies[].lootStones — number, in STONES (the currency, not raw mana stone) — actual coin or Guild credit taken off a person's body. The interface adds it straight to mana-stones once triggered; never state a person's purse total yourself.
enemies[].robbed — boolean. The second trigger, alongside conditionBand "down". Set it true the instant {{user}} takes a living person's belongings by force, threat, or theft — subdued, fled, surrendered, never actually killed. Don't set it for a pickpocket the person never notices unless {{user}} genuinely walks away with something; that's still a robbery.

WITNESS RISK — ENGINE-OWNED, not yours to narrate as certain either way. The instant a person reads as robbed and NOT down (isPerson:true, robbed:true or subdued, still alive), the interface privately rolls whether they got a good enough look to identify {{user}} later, and increments criminal-witnesses on a hit. You never set or read that number directly — a [UI] note tells you whether they lived clean or lived as a witness, and you narrate exactly that. Killing removes the risk entirely; that is the whole reason Bjorn's era treats it as the safer, uglier default, and citizen-status can flip to "wanted" from this alone with no input from you.

HARD DIRECTIVE-SAFETY RULE FOR THIS VARIABLE — NEVER WRITE THE WHOLE ENCOUNTER IN ONE DIRECTIVE. enemies is an array, and enemies[].loot is a SECOND array nested inside it — writing both in one [encounter-state: {...}] directive is a double-nested-bracket directive and WILL corrupt: it renders as raw broken JSON text directly in the chat the player reads, and it silently exposes hidden fields (loot, lootStones, isPerson, robbed) that must never reach the player. The only safe sequence is:
1. [encounter-state: merge {"active":true,"environment":"..."}] — scalars only, no enemies array yet.
2. [encounter-state.enemies: push {"name":"...","rankKnown":"?","conditionBand":"unharmed","isPerson":true}] — ONE enemy object per push, no loot field yet, repeat once per enemy.
3. Only once an enemy is genuinely down or robbed, and you know their array index (0 for the first pushed, 1 for the second...), push their loot ONE ITEM AT A TIME: [encounter-state.enemies.0.loot: push {"id":"...","name":"...","type":"...","qty":1,"description":"..."}], repeated once per item, then [encounter-state.enemies.0.lootStones: set N] as its own directive.
See directive-safety for the full worked example. This is not optional — it is the exact failure that has already leaked raw encounter JSON into the player's chat once.

variables.name: Discovered Map Nodes
variables.description: Persistent, discovery-based map data for the interactive map UI — surface districts and each Labyrinth floor as its own layer

surface.name: Karnon
surface.notes: The royal capital core. Palace of Glory and the ministries. Commoners cannot enter without permission.

surface.name: Magic Tower
surface.notes: The city-defining institution of the Wizards. No windows anywhere face the royal palace, by law.

surface.name: Gold Soul Repository
surface.notes: The palace's treasure vault, underground and windowless. Holds treasures up to rank-3 essences. Not open to citizens.

surface.name: Kommelby
surface.notes: Districts 2 through 5, the free market belt wrapped around Karnon. Artisans, shops, the city's middle class.

surface.name: Gnome Tree
surface.notes: District 6, the farming region, built on the Draconian tribe's holy land. Fairies work the fields here.

surface.name: Kiarbis
surface.notes: Residential resort district east of Gnome Tree's central mountain.

surface.name: Ravigion
surface.notes: Districts 7 through 13. Roughly seventy percent of the city lives here. Where you are now.

surface.name: the Dimensional Square
surface.notes: The portal into the Labyrinth. Opens at midnight on the first of every month. Every Ravigion district has one.

surface.name: Bifron
surface.notes: District 14. Prohibited. A former Ravigion zone whose Dimensional Square vanished. Believed less shielded from the Witch's poison. Called "the prison." People still live here.

variables.behaviorRules:
Object keyed by area id: "surface" for the city, "floor1".."floor10" for Labyrinth floors. Each key holds an array of node objects: { id (stable slug), name, type: one of "district","landmark","portal","rift","settlement","danger","altar", x (0-100), y (0-100), notes }.
Push a node ONLY when the player has genuinely discovered it — walked there, seen it from a vantage point, or been given a reliable, specific, in-world description (not vague rumor). Once a node's x/y is set, it is PERMANENT — never move it on a later push; if you need to add detail, update its notes field via merge instead of re-adding it. Coordinates are simulation-arbitrary but must stay internally consistent once established (Canon Discipline applies to any newly-generated floor region). Never populate a node for an area the player has not legitimately reached or reliably learned of — this variable drives what the map UI is allowed to reveal, and it must never leak GM knowledge.

THE SURFACE LAYER SHIPS PRE-SEEDED with the city's named districts — Karnon, Kommelby, Gnome Tree, Kiarbis, Ravigion, Bifron, the Dimensional Square, the Magic Tower, the Gold Soul Repository. This is baseline civic knowledge; any resident already knows the district map exists and roughly what each one is for, so it is not gated behind discovery the way specific buildings, shops, or Labyrinth floors still are. Do not re-add or move these nine — only ADD new surface nodes for specific places the player actually finds (a particular shop, a specific tavern, an NPC's home), and keep gating those the normal way. Labyrinth floor layers (floor1, floor2, ...) are entirely undiscovered by default and follow the original rule in full — nothing there is pre-known, ever.

variables.name: Mana Remaining
variables.description: Mana currently left in the pool. The pool's SIZE is the spirit variable — this is what remains in it. Read by the HUD and combat bar.
variables.behaviorRules:
How much mana is left in the pool right now. The pool's MAXIMUM is the spirit variable — this value must NEVER exceed it and never go below 0. If spirit rises, this does not automatically rise with it; mana is refilled by rest, not by growth.

Spend it only for things that genuinely run on mana: a fairy's elemental contract, a wizard's casting, an (A) essence ability that is explicitly magical, a beastman's summon. A barbarian swinging a shield spends stamina and never mana. Ordinary swings, sprints, climbs and shoves cost nothing here.

Typical costs: a minor effect 1-3, a solid combat ability 4-8, something that changes the shape of a fight 10+.

If the player attempts something that costs more mana than remains, IT DOES NOT HAPPEN. Do not let them overdraw, do not let it go negative, and do not quietly shrink the cost to make it fit. Narrate the failure physically — the gesture that produces nothing, the cold flat feeling of reaching for something that is not there — and let the round they wasted cost them.

At 0 the character is magically spent: no contract, no casting, no magical ability at all until they rest. Refills fully on a real night's sleep in a real bed, partially on a long sit-down rest.

variables.name: Stamina
variables.description: Exertion, separate from injury. Read by the HUD and the combat bar.
variables.behaviorRules:
Wind and exertion, entirely separate from injury. 100 = fresh. Never above 100, never below 0.

Spend 5-10 for a hard exchange of blows, 10-20 for a sprint or a climb, 15-30 for a forced march or a long fight, 20-40 for something desperate. A fight that costs no stamina did not happen.

Recovery: 20-40 on a long sit-down with water, full on a real night's sleep in a real bed. Nothing recovers on a march. Being injured slows recovery.

CONSEQUENCES AS IT FALLS — narrate these, do not announce numbers:
70-100 = breathing easy.
40-69 = winded; they would rather not run just now.
15-39 = the guard is dropping and they can feel it drop; accuracy and reaction suffer visibly.
1-14 = spent; everything is heavy, blocks arrive late, retreat is barely possible.
0 = they cannot fight, cannot run, and cannot lift the shield. Whatever happens next happens to them, not by them. This is how ordinary explorers die — not from one great blow but from having nothing left when the second goblin arrives.

variables.name: Time of Day
variables.description: Minutes since midnight, 0-1439. Wraps to a new day automatically.
variables.behaviorRules:
AUTHORITATIVE SURFACE TIME-OF-DAY CLOCK. Numeric minutes since midnight, 0–1439.

The engine automatically advances this clock by a 2-minute minimum on every active turn after character creation so ordinary conversation can never freeze time.

Then account for any ADDITIONAL duration needed for the actual action:
- brief exchange / a few spoken lines: about 2–5 minutes total
- ordinary conversation: about 5–20 minutes total
- long negotiation/interview: 15–45 minutes total
- quick inventory/equipment handling: 1–3 minutes total
- browsing/haggling/shop transaction: 10–30 minutes total
- walking locally: 5–25 minutes depending on distance
- crossing districts: 30–70 minutes
- meal: 20–40 minutes
- short fight: 1–10 minutes depending on actual sequence
- long fight/chase: 10–40+ minutes
- sleep/rest/travel: use their actual elapsed duration

Because 2 minutes are already added automatically, add only the EXTRA difference. Example: a 7-minute conversation turn receives automatic +2, then add +5.

Never keep the clock unchanged merely because the scene is dialogue. Speech, thinking, gestures, pauses, bargaining and walking all consume time.

The value is NUMERIC minutes, not a string. 300=05:00, 420=07:00, 780=13:00.

MIDNIGHT: if clock rises past 1439, clock-rollover subtracts 1440 and increments cycle-day. Do not separately double-increment the day.

Do not advance for a flashback or recap describing time that already passed. Do not double-charge UI actions that already explicitly advanced time.

variables.name: Day of Last Descent
variables.description: cycle-day value at the moment the player most recently entered the Labyrinth. 0 = not tracked / currently on the surface.
variables.behaviorRules: Set this to the CURRENT cycle-day the instant current-floor goes from 0 to anything above 0 — the moment the player descends. Leave it alone for the rest of the trip, however long that trip is narrated to be.

variables.name: Days Lived Inside
variables.description: Cumulative SUBJECTIVE days the character has spent inside the Labyrinth across the whole campaign — not calendar time.
variables.behaviorRules:
TIME DILATION. Canon states explorers age faster than calendar time: thirty ordinary days can mean thirty-seven days to four months of lived, aged, worn experience for someone who spends much of that time inside. This variable tracks the gap.

On EXIT from the Labyrinth (current-floor drops from >0 back to 0), add however many subjective days you narrated the trip taking — a quick in-and-out is +1, a real multi-day expedition might be +3 to +10, a months-long high-floor push (canon: some high-rank expeditions run nearly half a year subjectively) can be dozens. Be honest about it; do not round down to make the number look tidy.

SURFACE TIME DOES NOT MATCH IT. No matter how long the trip took inside, cycle-day advances by EXACTLY ONE from labyrinth-entry-day, and the player emerges around midday — set clock to 720. A three-day hunt and a three-week one both cost the surface world one calendar day. This is the whole mechanic: the character's own body and mind age on the LONGER, subjective clock, while Rafdonia only ever sees the short one.

Player-visible on the Sheet. Let the gap show up in prose too, especially once it's large — explorers who spend a lot of time on deep floors are known to look and act older than their years, tired in a way calendar age doesn't explain.

variables.name: Grind Session
variables.description: Live abstracted-grind run state, owned entirely by the interface resolver
variables.behaviorRules:
ENGINE-OWNED. You never write this. The interface's grind resolver fills it and hands you a [UI] note; your job is to narrate what it says happened.

Shape when a run is live: { active, floor, intent ("stones" | "essence" | "portal" | "plunder" | "survive"), daysOrdered, daysSpent, daysBanked, kills (object keyed by species -> count), stones, essencesFound, firstKills (array), riftsSeen, partiesMet, status ("running" | "interrupted" | "complete" | "aborted"), interrupt (object: { kind, what, where, detail }) }.

HOW TO NARRATE IT:
- status "complete": a compressed montage of the whole stretch. Days blurring, the specific ugly texture of repetition, what the body feels like at the end. State the totals plainly at the close. Do not dramatize numbers upward.
- status "interrupted": STOP the montage at the interrupt. Put {{user}} in that exact moment, in present tense, and end there on the decision. Never resolve the interrupt for them.
- status "aborted": the run ended early on a hard stop (deadline, collapse, floor closing). Narrate the reason as it physically happened.

Never invent kills, stones, drops, or encounters that are not in this object. Never round the numbers up. If it says four days of nothing, four days of nothing is the scene.

variables.name: Days Left On This Floor
variables.description: In-floor (subjective) days remaining before the current floor spits everyone out. 0 on the surface.
variables.behaviorRules:
ENGINE-OWNED — you never set this. Measured in IN-FLOOR days, the clock the Labyrinth itself keeps, not Rafdonia's calendar.

Set on descent from the floor's fixed budget, burned down by grind resolution and by narrated day passage. Floors 1-5 only; floors 6 and deeper run their own continuous clock and this reads 0 there.

NARRATE THE PRESSURE, NOT THE NUMBER. Nobody down there has a countdown. They have the way other explorers start moving toward the portals, the way a camp thins out overnight, someone loudly counting sleeps at a fire. At 2 days or fewer the mood on the floor should be visibly wrong. At 0, the floor spits everyone still inside back to the surface — that is not negotiable and not survivable to resist.

variables.name: Portal Search Progress
variables.description: How close the player is to locating the descent portal on the current floor. Resets on floor change.
variables.behaviorRules:
ENGINE-OWNED — you never set this directly. Rises two ways only: the grind "portal" intent, or a pushed search-log claim resolved by PortalSearch. NEVER raise it by writing the number yourself for a narrated search — that channel is disabled on purpose. Resets to 0 on arriving at a new floor.

EXPECT MULTIPLE SEARCHES PER FLOOR, NOT ONE. A single claim grants roughly 35-55 points on Floor 1, dropping to roughly 6-12 on Floor 5 — deeper floors are bigger and better hidden, and take real, repeated investment to search out. One search scene should almost never be the whole story.

NEVER STATE THIS AS A PERCENTAGE. There is no progress bar in the Labyrinth. Express it as ground covered and landmarks ruled out: which directions are exhausted, which monument was already found dead, how much of the terrain still looks the same in every direction. Low values mean genuinely lost. At 100 the portal is in sight — say so plainly and let them choose whether to take it.

Remember Floor 2's rule: eight portal monuments, and opening one turns the other seven to stone. Someone else finding it first can erase progress that was real.

variables.name: Mana Stones (Pouch)
variables.description: Physical mana stones cut from corpses, carried in a pouch, keyed by species. Not money — only a Guild counter converts them into stones.
variables.behaviorRules:
ENGINE-OWNED — you never write this. The Oracle, the grind resolver and the Guild exchange counter are the only things that touch it.

WHAT IT HOLDS: mana stones. Physical loot, cut out of monster corpses, keyed by species — { "Goblin": { rank: 9, qty: 12 } }. There is no other name for them; never call them "raw stones" or "raw haul". They are mana stones, and they are heavy, obvious, and worth nothing across any counter in Rafdonia.

THE ONLY CONVERSION: an Explorers' Guild exchange counter on the surface grades the pouch by rank, weighs it, records it, handles the city's tax deduction, and pays out in STONES (the mana-stones variable) minus the Guild's fee. Nowhere else. No shop, no merchant, no black market, no underground buyer takes mana stones across a counter.

NARRATION: refer to the contents as mana stones. Say the pouch is heavy. Never state a currency total for what is in it — {{user}}'s panel shows an appraisal ESTIMATE only, and the Guild's offer at the counter is the real number. Never narrate {{user}} as having been paid before they physically reach a counter.

variables.name: Witnesses Left Alive
variables.description: Engine-only counter: robbed-but-living people who may identify the player later.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE-OWNED, never touched by AI directives (aiAccess none, invisible to game-state). Incremented by the Oracle exactly when a robbed person is left alive and a witness roll hits. Watched by behaviors: each increment nudges fame up slightly (being talked about raises how known the player is, which per fame's own rule also pushes suspicion upward), and crossing 3 flips citizen-status to 'wanted' on its own, no AI input. Never reset manually — one-way ledger, same spirit as suspicion.

variables.name: Vault Balance
variables.description: Legacy aggregate of all Alminus-held currency: registered-vault-balance + unregistered-vault-balance.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE/UI-OWNED compatibility aggregate. The Vault UI keeps this equal to the sum of both vault balances. Do not treat it as a third account.

variables.name: Bank Account
variables.description: Legacy Alminus account compatibility metadata.
variables.behaviorRules: Compatibility only. New vault logic uses vault-access and the separate registered/unregistered balances and item lists.

variables.name: Party
variables.description: The explorers currently travelling with {{user}}. Five slots, {{user}} included.
variables.behaviorRules:
READ-ONLY TO YOU. The interface's party panel adds and removes members; you never write this array. A full party is FIVE including {{user}}, so four slots are recruitable. Each member: name, rank (9 lowest to 1 apex), race, age, class, role, plus notes and a wage or share arrangement. Optional: wayfinding (boolean) — set true ONLY when this specific person's real background is trail work, tracking, or scouting (a Fairy dispatched to Gnome Tree, a Beastman with a hunting lineage, a veteran guide) and say so in their notes. This is a genuine, felt bonus to finding a way through a floor — never set it for convenience, and most recruits should not have it. A member with the Navigation skill (see Trainable Skills) automatically counts as wayfinding-capable too — don't set both fields, the interface treats Navigation as covering it. Optional: skills (array of skill OBJECTS, same shape as the player's own skills variable — {name, stage, proficiency}, not bare strings) — zero, one, rarely two, matching this person's actual race and class. A recruit worth having usually sits Novice or Intermediate, not fresh Barely Formed and not an implausible Master. Most recruits, like most essences, are ordinary and carry none at all. Never give a recruit Paladin (it doesn't use this stage/proficiency shape at all — see paladin-standing) or Priest of the Karui (a rare, dangerous, story-weight class that should never appear as a casual recruit trait) unless the scene has genuinely, deliberately earned it. These are people, not equipment — they have their own tax due, their own quota, their own opinion of where the party is hunting, and they will refuse an order that reads as suicide. Reference them by name in narration whenever the party is together; if a member is present, they act. A member who dies in the Labyrinth stays dead, and someone has to tell whoever they were feeding.

COMBAT STATE: every member may also carry id, combatRole, equipment, and combat:{condition,conditionMax,stamina,staminaMax,mana,manaMax,status,injuries}. These are engine-owned persistent combat resources. You still do not write party directly; report established companion combat outcomes through party-combat-events.

COMPANION SHEET FIELDS: inventory (same physical item objects as player inventory), essences (same essence object grammar: source/rank/weight/abilities/statBoost/statMods), essenceCapacity, combatRole, and combat resources. Recruitment should preserve any established gear/essences instead of flattening them to biography text.

AUTONOMOUS LIFE: each member also owns personality, personalStones, and lifeState. personality contains aggression/caution/discipline/altruism/independence/frugality/ambition/loyalty (0–100 simulation values) plus optional traits/fears/likes/dislikes/combatStyle. personalStones are THEIR money, not the player's mana-stones. On ordinary Rafdonia surface days, the engine may let them independently train, socialize, save, pursue errands, or buy plausible gear with their own money. Their purchases enter their own inventory and can be equipped automatically. Never charge the player's purse for these independent choices.

PERSISTENT LIFE STATE: lifeState additionally owns goals, plans, obligations, relationships, privateKnowledge, knownToPlayer, history and lastProcessedOrdinal. Private fields are simulation truth but are not automatically player knowledge. Catch-up simulation advances elapsed surface days; recent days are resolved individually and older low-detail spans may be aggregated.

variables.name: Recruiting
variables.description: Engine-facing recruitment UI state: Guild listings plus the current individual prospect.
variables.behaviorRules:
The runtime owns individual prospect state. Do not rely on fragile recruit-state.prospect merge syntax after an NPC agrees. Instead append recruitment-events type:'eligible'; the engine synchronizes the NPC actor and exposes RECRUIT.

Guild board listings may still be populated when the player actually reads a recruitment board. Listings are advertisements, not consent.

Prospect fields may include {active,status,eligible,actorId,name,rank,race,age,class,role,fee,notes,skills,equipment,inventory,essences,essenceCapacity,background,stats,personality,personalStones,lifeState,combat}. status='eligible' or eligible=true means explicit consent has already happened. Never write party directly.

variables.name: Gear Taken From People
variables.description: Provenance ledger for equipment taken off people rather than monsters. Separate from inventory, which only records what is carried.
variables.behaviorRules:
A PROVENANCE LEDGER, not a second inventory. The interface moves the actual object into inventory; this records where it CAME FROM, because that is what can hang {{user}}.

Push one object per piece of gear taken off a person — killed, robbed, or looted from a corpse {{user}} did not make. ONE PUSH AT A TIME, never an inline array:
[hot-goods: push {"item": "Moonstone-edged arming sword", "from": "the Sawtooth scout", "distinct": "high", "witnesses": "her two companions ran", "laundered": false}]

FIELDS:
- item — must match the name used in inventory exactly, or the two ledgers drift apart.
- from — whose it was. A name if {{user}} learned it, a description if not. "unknown Rank 9 in a green cloak" is fine.
- distinct — how identifiable the piece is, and this is the whole mechanic. "low" = common issue, a plain iron blade, a used shield, nothing anybody could pick out of a crowd. "medium" = good quality, clan-adjacent, a smith might recognise his own work. "high" = engraved, clan-marked, custom-fitted, a Numbered Item, or something whose owner was locally known. Judge it honestly at the moment it is taken; do not soften it later.
- witnesses — plain text describing who saw and whether they lived. "none, all three died" is a genuinely different situation from "one ran".
- laundered — false on acquisition. Set true only after it has actually been disposed of through a channel that breaks the trail (black market, a fence, reforging at a smithy that asks nothing, a sealed auction lot). Selling a "high" piece over an ordinary counter does NOT launder it — it does the opposite.

REMOVE an entry when the item genuinely leaves {{user}}'s hands for good: [hot-goods: delete item='Moonstone-edged arming sword'].

WHAT THIS DRIVES: a "high" piece sold or worn openly is how plunderers get caught — see the Elbis precedent. The world reacts to the OBJECT, not to a number: a smith who goes quiet and long in the face, a clerk who copies the registration twice, someone at the next table who knew the dead woman's sword. Never state this ledger's contents to {{user}} as a list. They know what they took; they do not know who is going to recognise it.

variables.name: Property Held
variables.description: Every place {{user}} rents or owns — residences and commercial units alike.
variables.behaviorRules:
ENGINE-OWNED — the interface's Home panel adds, alters and removes these. You never write to it. You narrate what it says.

Each entry: { id (stable string), name, district (Karnon/Kommelby/Gnome Tree/Kiarbis/Ravigion/Bifron), kind ("residence" or "commercial"), tenure ("rented" or "owned"), rent (stones per month, 0 if owned outright), price (what it cost, if bought), condition (short phrase — "sound", "damp", "one window boarded"), notes, tenantRent (stones per month if sublet to someone else, 0 otherwise), business (object or null).

A business object: { trade (e.g. "variety store", "smithy stall", "pub", "boarding house", "workshop"), staff (number), upkeep (stones per month), takings (stones last month), notes }.

HOW TO NARRATE IT: a rented room in Ravigion is a door with a lock and a landlord who counts days. An owned house in Kommelby is a genuine asset and a genuine target. Bifron is cheap because it is Bifron. A place has a smell, a stair that complains, neighbours who notice a body coming home at odd hours — and that last one matters enormously for an Evil Spirit. Property is the single best thing {{user}} can do to look like a person who belongs here, and the single worst thing to have when they need to disappear.

NEVER invent a property into this array in prose. If {{user}} wants somewhere, that goes through the board or through asking around, and the interface writes it.

variables.name: Where You Sleep
variables.description: The id of the property {{user}} currently lives in. Empty means no fixed address.
variables.behaviorRules:
ENGINE-OWNED — set by the interface's Home panel. You never write it.

Empty string means {{user}} has NO fixed address: motels at roughly 9,000 stones a night in Kommelby, cheaper and worse further out, or a floor somewhere, or nowhere. That is the default state and it is expensive in a slow bleed — a month of motel nights costs more than most rooms cost to rent.

When it holds an id, that is where {{user}} actually sleeps, and resting there is free. Match the narration to that property's district and condition.

Having no address is also a mild social liability: a landlord, a Guild clerk, or a neighbour asking "where are you living?" and getting no answer is exactly the kind of small wrongness that gets remembered.

variables.name: Deposit Box Contents
variables.description: Legacy aggregate view of all objects lodged at Alminus across registered and unregistered boxes.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE/UI-OWNED compatibility aggregate. The Vault UI keeps this equal to registered-vault-items + unregistered-vault-items. Do not treat it as a third box.

variables.name: Property Listings
variables.description: Live property listings for the Home panel's search board — you populate, the interface reads.
variables.behaviorRules:
YOU POPULATE THIS, the interface reads it and does the money.

Object: { boardActive (boolean), source (e.g. "district administrative agency", "a notice wall in Kommelby", "a broker in Kiarbis"), listings (array) }.

Each listing: { id (stable string), name, district, kind ("residence" or "commercial"), tenure ("rented" or "owned"), rent (stones/month, 0 if for sale), price (stones to buy, 0 if rental only), condition (short phrase), notes (one honest line — what is wrong with it, who the landlord is, what the street is like).

ARRAY SAFETY: set the scalars first with merge, then push listings ONE AT A TIME.
[property-market: merge {"boardActive":true,"source":"..."}]
[property-market.listings: push {"id":"...","name":"...","district":"...","kind":"residence","tenure":"rented","rent":4200,"price":0,"condition":"damp","notes":"..."}]

PRICE IT HONESTLY, off the 20-stone loaf. Rough monthly rent: Bifron 800-2,000 (and it is Bifron). Ravigion 3,000-9,000. Gnome Tree 4,000-11,000. Kiarbis 15,000-40,000. Kommelby 18,000-60,000. Karnon does not rent to commoners at all. Purchase runs roughly 90-130 months of the same place's rent. Commercial units cost 1.5-3x a residence of the same size in the same district, and a unit with an existing fitted trade costs more again.

POST 3-6 LISTINGS, never a clean sweep of good ones. At least one should be genuinely bad — a boarded window, a landlord who wants three months up front, a neighbour problem, a unit whose last tenant left in a hurry and nobody will say why. Rank and notoriety change what a landlord will even show {{user}}, and a Barbarian body gets fewer doors opened in Kommelby than a human one.

Clear boardActive to false once {{user}} walks away from the board.

variables.name: Property Ledger
variables.description: Engine bookkeeping for monthly rent, tenant income and business takings.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE-ONLY. Never in the prompt, never touched by directives. The interface settles rent owed, tenant income and business takings once per month and records what it moved here so it cannot double-charge inside the same month.

variables.name: Kill Claims (Narration → Engine)
variables.description: The channel narration uses to report a kill to the Oracle. You push a claim; the engine pays it out.
variables.behaviorRules:
THE KILL CHANNEL. This is how a kill you NARRATE actually reaches the engine.

WHY THIS EXISTS: you are not permitted to write raw-stones, and the engine DROPS that directive silently — so a kill written in prose can read as fully resolved and change nothing at all. Never try to write raw-stones, and never state a mana stone was pouched without a claim here. Push a claim instead and the Oracle does the mana stone, the achievement point, the first-kill check and the essence roll itself, at the real rates, and reports back in a [UI] note.

PUSH ONE CLAIM PER KILL, IN THE SAME MESSAGE AS THE NARRATION:
[kill-log: push {"name":"Tyrant Tarunbas","qty":1,"guardian":true}]

FIELDS:
- name (required) — the species name exactly as the bestiary registry spells it. Spelling is what the rank lookup keys on; a misspelling earns no achievement points.
- qty — how many of that same species died. Default 1. Use it to report a stretch honestly: three goblins is one claim with qty 3, not three claims.
- guardian — true ONLY for a genuine Rift Guardian. The loot math is completely different (33% essence) and this is the only signal the engine gets. Never a guess.
- isPerson — true for an explorer, bandit, guard, anyone with a name and a life. Turns off ALL monster math: no essence, no mana stone, no achievement, ever. Pair with loot (array of item objects) and lootStones (a number, in currency) for what they were carrying.
- rank — ONLY for a monster you invented that is not in the registry. If the registry knows the name, omit this; the registry wins.
- force — true ONLY when resolving a [sync] or [add:] repair for a kill that was never paid out. Without it, a claim naming something the combat panel already paid is refused as a duplicate.

DO NOT ALSO WRITE: achievements, species-killed, essences, essence-capacity, level, or soul-power for a kill you have claimed here. The engine writes all of them. Writing them yourself double-pays and corrupts the sheet. Levels and capacity follow from achievement points on their own.

ONE CHANNEL PER KILL. If the enemy was in encounter-state and you marked it down there, the Oracle already paid it — do not also claim it here. If the fight happened purely in prose, claim it here. Never both.

You never set resolved; the engine does.

variables.name: Repair Claims (Sync → Engine)
variables.description: The channel [sync] uses to repair anything engine-owned that never landed. Not for kills — those go through kill-log.
variables.behaviorRules:
THE REPAIR CHANNEL. Use ONLY while resolving a [sync], [sync all] or [add: X] command — never during ordinary narration.

WHY IT EXISTS: many variables refuse your directives outright (raw-stones, mana-stones arithmetic the engine owns, bank-balance, registered-vault-balance, unregistered-vault-balance, portal-progress, floor-days-left, party, properties, home-current, vault-items, bank-account, criminal-witnesses, property-ledger, grind-session). A directive to those is DISCARDED SILENTLY — the narration reads as though it worked and the sheet never moves. Re-issuing it during a [sync] fails identically, forever. Push a repair claim here instead and the engine applies it and reports back in a [UI] note.

SHAPE — one push per correction, never an inline array of them:
[repair-log: push {"target":"mana-stones","op":"add","value":4500,"reason":"sold the iron sword, payment never landed"}]

target — the variable id to correct.
op — "add" (default) | "subtract" | "set" | "remove" (arrays only) | "merge" (objects).
value — a number for numeric targets; an object (or array of objects) for list targets; for raw-stones an object {"name":"Goblin","rank":9,"qty":3}.
reason — short plain-English note on what the narration said should have happened.

REPAIRABLE NUMBERS: mana-stones, human-kills, bank-balance, achievements, portal-progress, floor-days-left, criminal-witnesses, labyrinth-days, labyrinth-entry-day, soul-power, essence-capacity, level, spirit-current, explorer-rank, tax-owed, fame, suspicion.
REPAIRABLE LISTS (op add/remove/set): inventory, vault-items, registered-vault-items, unregistered-vault-items, properties, party, species-killed, essences, hot-goods, numbered-items, injuries, quest-log, floors-seen.
REPAIRABLE OBJECTS (op merge/set): raw-stones, bank-account, vault-access, reputation, knowledge, map-knowledge.
REPAIRABLE STRINGS (op set): home-current, location, citizen-status, char-name.

DO NOT use this for a missed KILL — a kill's mana stone, achievement point and essence roll all have to come from one dice pass. Push to kill-log with force:true instead and let the engine pay the whole thing.

DO NOT use this for state you can already write normally — condition, thirst, stamina, clock, cycle-day, current-floor, shop-state, current-npc, encounter-state, reputation prose, injuries during live play. An ordinary directive works there; use one.

The engine refuses unknown targets and tells you so. If a repair claim is refused, say so plainly to the player instead of inventing a workaround.

loot-resolution-ledger is intentionally NOT ordinarily repairable through prose. It is engine bookkeeping that prevents double payment. Do not clear it to force a second payout.

variables.name: Search Claims
variables.description: Claim channel for a narrated portal-search action. See kill-log for the identical pattern.
variables.behaviorRules:
THE PORTAL SEARCH CHANNEL. This is how a narrated search actually reaches the engine — you cannot write portal-progress directly, and the engine drops that write silently.

Push exactly one claim per genuine search scene, in the same message as the narration:
[search-log: push {"note": "spent the day working the east wall for a way down"}]

WRITE THE SCENE LIKE IT TOOK HOURS, BECAUSE IT DID. A single claim represents real, physical time on real ground — a corridor that looks like the last three, a wrong turn retraced, the light changing, legs and lungs feeling it. Never resolve a search in one sentence. Describe distance covered, landmarks ruled out one at a time, the size of the place working against the player, and only THEN push the claim. The [UI] note that comes back tells you the real outcome — narrate that honestly, but the journey there is yours to write in full, and it should read like it earned whatever the note says.

The watcher resolves a real, floor-scaled, dice-backed gain — never a flat number you choose, never a jump straight to 100. It also costs real thirst, real stamina, and a day off the floor's own clock, and reports back in a [UI] note. Narrate what that note says; do not also describe the portal as found unless it explicitly says so.

A single search scene is ONE claim, however long the prose describing it runs. Do not push more than one claim per scene to inflate the gain.

You never set resolved; the engine does.

variables.name: Trained Skills
variables.description: The player's own learned, non-essence skills — Auror, Spellcraft, Divine Power, Necromancy, Navigation.
variables.behaviorRules:
THE SKILL LIST IS FIXED, NOT INVENTED. Auror, Spellcraft, Divine Power, Necromancy, Navigation, Warrior, Archer, Spearman, Martial Artist, Boxer, Samurai, Summoner, Warlock, Berserker, Alchemist, Knight, Paladin, and — rare and dangerous, see the Trainable Skills entry before ever using it — Priest of the Karui. See the Trainable Skills entry for what each one actually is. Never register a skill outside that catalog; there is no open-ended discovery mechanic here.

PALADIN IS THE ONE EXCEPTION TO EVERYTHING BELOW — it never uses this stage/proficiency ladder at all. See paladin-standing for its real, separate mechanic.

BUT ONCE A SKILL IS TRAINED, IT PROGRESSES ON A REAL LADDER. Push a new skill only after real, narrated training completes:
[skills: push {"name": "Auror", "stage": "Barely Formed", "proficiency": 0, "trainedAt": "cycle 3"}]

STAGE LADDER — fixed order, never invent alternate names: Barely Formed -> Novice -> Intermediate -> Adept -> Master -> Sovereign.

PROFICIENCY IS PER-STAGE, NOT ONE CONTINUOUS 0-100 SCALE. It always represents progress toward COMPLETING the current stage, never overall mastery. A skill does not drift from 22% to 45% and relabel itself — the current stage must fully complete (proficiency reaches 100) before advancing.

HOW TO ADVANCE:
1. A newly trained skill starts at Barely Formed, proficiency 0.
2. Raise proficiency +3 to +12 per real training session or genuinely meaningful use in the fiction — never regresses, never resets on its own, persists across sessions untouched for weeks.
3. When proficiency reaches 100 at any stage before Master: advance stage to the next name on the ladder AND reset proficiency to 0, in the same directive batch. The skill is now at the START of the new stage, not carrying leftover progress.
4. THE ONE EXCEPTION — Master to Sovereign. Reaching proficiency 100 at Master is necessary but NOT sufficient. Only promote to Sovereign when the number hits 100 AND a real narrative breakthrough happens in that same scene (a fight it saved them in, a teacher confirming it, a moment it visibly clicks). If the breakthrough hasn't landed, hold the skill at Master, proficiency 100, until the fiction earns it. Never auto-advance on the number alone — the Skills panel will show it waiting.

WHAT EACH STAGE MEANS IN PLAY, narrate consistently with wherever a skill currently sits:
Barely Formed — high failure risk, severe inefficiency, real chance of backlash.
Novice — usable, but unreliable the moment real pressure shows up.
Intermediate — dependable, as long as conditions stay favourable.
Adept — dependable even under pressure.
Master — near second nature.
Sovereign — total mastery, exceedingly rare; most explorers never see one on anyone, ever.

OPTIONAL DISCIPLINE LADDER — a small number of skills (Spellcraft is the natural candidate) can carry an internal, separate 3-5 rung ladder tracking a specific sub-discipline, independent of the overall stage above: discipline: [{"name":"...","desc":"...","unlocked":false}, ...]. Only unlock a rung when proficiency crosses a real threshold AND the fiction shows the actual breakthrough — never for pacing. This is optional; most skills don't need it.

One or two trained skills per character is realistic; more strains belief. See Trainable Skills for gating (Auror is Human-only, no exception) and training cost.

EFFECTIVENESS IS REAL AND CODE-COMPUTED — read it, don't invent a different one. The Skills panel shows a tier (struggling / uneven / solid / strong / exceptional / overwhelming) combining a skill's stage and proficiency with whatever Physique substat actually bears on it: Auror reads Strength and Accuracy Rate, Navigation reads Vision and Sense of Smell, Spellcraft reads Vision. Divine Power and Necromancy have no substat tie at all — nothing in canon makes spellwork or dark ritual depend on a physical stat, so don't invent one.

WHAT THIS GOVERNS AND WHAT IT DOESN'T. This tier decides how GOOD a specific use of a trained skill reads — a Sovereign-tier Auror strike should land clean and hard where a Barely-Formed one should be clumsy, half-charged, maybe backfire. It does NOT decide who wins a fight, whether an enemy dies, or replace your own judgment about the scene. Combat outcome stays entirely yours to narrate — this only tells you how much the trained skill itself is pulling its weight in that outcome. A 'struggling' Auror can still win a fight through luck, numbers, or the enemy's own mistake; an 'overwhelming' one can still lose to something genuinely worse. Never state the tier as a number to the player — describe it: clean or clumsy, precise or wasted, controlled or barely holding together.

RUNTIME UPDATE CONTRACT — DO NOT LEAVE TRAINING AS FLAVOR TEXT:
When a scene materially changes a trained skill, update this variable in the same turn.
- Completing the weeks-long initial training for one of the five valid paths -> push the new skill at Barely Formed / 0 proficiency.
- Completing a real practice session or making genuinely meaningful use under pressure -> add an earned +3 to +12 proficiency to that specific skill.
- If that addition reaches or exceeds 100 before Master -> advance exactly one stage and reset proficiency to the appropriate remainder within the new stage; never skip a stage.
- At Master 100, hold there until the required narrative breakthrough actually occurs; then promote to Sovereign.
- If an optional discipline rung's threshold and fictional breakthrough are both met, mark that rung unlocked in the same update.
- Do not grant progress merely because time passed, the player clicked the Skills screen, or the narrator wants faster pacing.

The Skills screen is a VIEW of these consequences, not the cause of them. Teachers, practice, cost, aptitude, danger, and time remain physical events in Rafdonia.

variables.name: Official Team Status
variables.description: Whether the current party has been formally registered as an official team at the Explorers' Guild.
variables.behaviorRules:
CANON-CONFIRMED, TWO REAL STAGES — do not collapse them into one. Finding people to team up with (the Board or a Prospect) is informal and needs nothing further; an ad-hoc group can hunt together, split loot at a pub, and do everything ordinary explorers do without ever touching this variable.

BUT source states plainly: once a real team has actually come together, it must be registered as an OFFICIAL team at the Guild — this is a separate, deliberate administrative act, not automatic. No exact requirements survive in the source beyond that fact, so these are reasonable, consistent, LOCKED simulation canon, not literal transcription: every member must already be individually registered (explorer-rank above 0 — an unregistered person cannot be added to an official roster), the whole group presents together or is accounted for at a Guild branch, and a modest one-time paperwork fee is paid (a few thousand stones, not a real barrier — this is bureaucracy, not a gate).

SET TRUE only after that scene is actually played out. WHAT CHANGES: only a registered team is eligible for Guild-brokered contracts and requests (see Income Reality), is the unit the Guild tracks for disaster relief if something goes wrong in the Labyrinth, and is who the recurring first-to-open-portal credit and Numbered-Item dispute customs formally recognise as a party rather than a crowd of individuals who happened to be nearby. An unregistered group gets none of that — they can still hunt together, they just aren't a team as far as the Guild's own paperwork is concerned.

Resets to false if the roster changes meaningfully (a member leaves, someone new joins) until the GM narrates re-registering — the Guild's records reflect who is actually on the team, not who used to be.

variables.name: Personal Titles
variables.description: Personal-scale firsts and real accomplishments — the individual counterpart to the city-wide Honor Stone.
variables.behaviorRules:
PERSONAL SCALE, NOT CITY SCALE. The Honor Stone records legendary, city-wide firsts — new floor discoveries, feats that make the history books. This is smaller and much more common: a real, earned first for THIS PERSON specifically, the kind of thing that gets repeated at a pub even if nobody outside the party remembers it in a year.

Push only after something real actually happens in the fiction — never for reaching a number, never for pacing:
[titles: push {"name": "Liakis-Touched", "earnedAt": "cycle 4, day 9", "note": "stood in the Witch's Forest when the Lord of Chaos passed within sight and lived to talk about it"}]

WHAT EARNS ONE: surviving something that kills most people who face it, a first kill of a named or exceptional threat, a feat a party or clan genuinely talks about afterward, the kind of thing a recruiter or a stranger at a pub might recognise the name for. NOT: reaching a level, finishing a grind, routine success. Most explorers, even successful ones, hold one or two of these across a whole career, not a shelf of them.

Titles carry no numeric bonus — their effect is entirely social and narrative: recognition, a story that precedes the character, sometimes unwanted attention. Never invent a mechanical bonus for one.

variables.name: Living World State
variables.description: Persistent macro and district-level state of Rafdonia and the currently relevant Labyrinth/world.
variables.behaviorRules:
ENGINE LEDGER. Maintain only facts that materially affect future play. District records may contain population pressure, security, shortages, closures, disasters, public mood, traffic, and other persistent conditions grounded in lore or events.

Do not invent sweeping world changes without a cause. Every non-canon condition should be traceable to world-events or consequence-ledger. Use stable keys. Update lastSimulatedClock whenever a meaningful offscreen simulation pass occurs.

variables.name: Persistent NPC Ledger
variables.description: Persistent records for named NPCs who matter to the simulation, whether canon or generated.
variables.behaviorRules:
Engine-authoritative object keyed by stable actor id/slug. EVERY named or materially interactive person may persist here whether or not they are recruitable. Records may include {id,name,provenance,race,age,affiliation,role,occupation,background,location,home,alive,condition,stamina,staminaMax,rank,personality,stats,skills,essences,inventory,equipment,personalStones,goals,plans,obligations,relationships,knowledge,beliefs,memories,privateKnowledge,knownToPlayer,scheduleState,businessState,simLevel,lastSeenClock,lastProcessedOrdinal}. simLevel 1 = brief encounter persistence; 2 = recurring NPC with offscreen life catch-up; 3 = major/canon/relationship NPC with deeper continuity. Hidden stats/personality/background/private knowledge are simulation truth, NOT automatically player knowledge. Established canon/authored facts override generated defaults. NPCs are people, not quest objects. They remember only witnessed or reliably learned events; they do not know hidden facts merely because the engine does.

RECRUITMENT STATE: actor records may include recruitment:{status:'none|negotiating|eligible|recruited|declined|withdrawn',terms,notes,lastChangedClock}. Only explicit fictional consent makes an actor eligible.

variables.name: Organizations and Factions
variables.description: Persistent state for clans, Guild branches, churches, noble houses, criminal groups, businesses, parties, and other organizations.
variables.behaviorRules:
Stable slug -> {name, provenance, type, headquarters, leaders[], membersBand, resourcesBand, goals[], rivals[], allies[], territories[], publicStance, privatePriorities[], playerStanding, knowledge{}, currentProjects[], lastUpdatedClock}.

Seed organizations from lore as they become relevant; never replace canon structure with generic fantasy factions. Organizations act through people, resources, rules, and information. A faction cannot retaliate for a secret act it has not learned about. Leadership changes persist. Resource losses matter. Territory, membership, and political influence can change through causal events.

variables.name: Dynamic Economy
variables.description: Supply, demand, price pressure, merchant liquidity, shortages, and market shocks by district and commodity.
variables.behaviorRules:
LORE-BASED ECONOMY. Canon prices and known economic facts are anchors. Do not randomly drift them without material cause.

For each relevant commodity use:
{basePrice, supplyIndex, demandIndex, scarcityIndex, districtIndex, shockIndex, currentReferencePrice, lastUpdatedClock, causes[]}

Reference price formula:
currentReferencePrice = round(basePrice * supplyIndex * demandIndex * scarcityIndex * districtIndex * shockIndex)

Normal indices hover near 1.00. Changes require causes such as Labyrinth closure/opening, explorer casualties, a discovered route, monster-material influx, destroyed stock, war, guild procurement, hoarding, crime, taxation, transport disruption, or player dumping/withholding a meaningful quantity.

A single poor explorer selling three swords does not move a city market. A clan unloading wagonloads might. Prices can differ by district. Individual merchants may deviate from the reference price based on inventory, cash, disposition, risk, quality, and negotiation.

Whenever shop-state is populated, derive prices from canon/base item value plus economy-state rather than inventing a disconnected price.

LIVING ECONOMY: economy-state summarizes macro facts; market-index is the executable aggregate price state. Changes require causal supply/demand. Track categories, not every object. Exact canon numbers always override simulation baselines.

variables.name: Political State
variables.description: Offices, influence, active issues, institutional conflicts, and political consequences.

variables.name: Rumors and Public Information
variables.description: Tracks rumors separately from truth, including source, reach, distortion, and who knows them.
variables.behaviorRules:
A rumor is not truth and truth is not automatically public.

Rumor object:
{id, claim, truthStatus:'true'|'false'|'mixed'|'unknown', origin, carriers[], locations[], organizations[], reach:0-100, credibility:0-100, distortionNotes[], createdClock, lastSpreadClock, status:'active'|'faded'|'confirmed'|'disproved'}

Create rumors only when information could actually spread: witnesses, survivors, merchants, guild reports, taverns, clan channels, churches, officials, newspapers/notices if lore supports them, etc.

Reach grows through carriers and travel, not because turns passed. Credibility changes with source quality and corroboration. Details can distort. A secret action with no surviving witness and no material evidence does not create a public rumor.

Player reputation and suspicion may respond to what people BELIEVE, not only what is objectively true.

variables.name: World Event Ledger
variables.description: Scheduled, active, and resolved events that occur independently of the player.
variables.behaviorRules:
Event object:
{id, provenance, type, title, location, actors[], startClock, deadlineClock, prerequisites[], resources{}, publicVisibility, state, effects[], parentEventId|null}

Seed canon-era events when their prerequisites and timing become relevant. Generated events must emerge from lore systems: Labyrinth cycles, monster activity, clan competition, crime, trade, institutional duties, accidents, politics, personal NPC goals, or consequences of prior events.

Events continue without {{user}} when logically possible. Do not pause the world waiting for them. Resolve offscreen at appropriate abstraction. If {{user}} intervenes, use their actual actions and resulting state. Never preserve a canonical outcome after its prerequisites have been destroyed.
PLAYER VISIBILITY: WORLD UI displays an event only if publicVisibility is true or player knowledge has a recorded causal route. Hidden active events must not leak merely because they exist.

variables.name: Causal Consequence Ledger
variables.description: Tracks unresolved and resolved consequences created by player and world actions.
variables.behaviorRules:
Whenever a meaningful act changes the world, record only consequences that have a plausible carrier.

Pending consequence:
{id, cause, actor, target, scope:'personal'|'local'|'organizational'|'market'|'political'|'historical', knowledgeRoute, materialRoute, earliestClock, likelihoodBand, state, effects[]}

knowledgeRoute explains how people could learn it.
materialRoute explains how physical/economic effects propagate.

No route = no propagated consequence. Direct physical consequences may be immediate. Social consequences wait for information. Market consequences require meaningful quantity/supply/demand impact. Political consequences require stakeholders and leverage.

When resolved, move the record to resolved with the actual outcome. Do not keep spawning recursive consequences forever; stop once effects become negligible.

variables.name: Canon Timeline and Divergence
variables.description: Tracks the Bjorn-era baseline and any causal divergences created by the simulation.
variables.behaviorRules:
Canon is the default timeline, not destiny.

Anchor object:
{id, canonEvent, expectedWindow, prerequisites[], actors[], state:'pending'|'preserved'|'altered'|'invalidated'}

Divergence object:
{id, clock, cause, affectedAnchors[], severity:1-5, summary}

When a canon-relevant prerequisite is changed, update the affected anchor. If the old event can still happen naturally, preserve it. If its cause, actor, location, resource, death, alliance, or decision has materially changed, alter or invalidate it. Increase divergenceLevel only for changes that genuinely affect broader historical trajectories.

Never contrive events to push history back onto rails.

variables.name: Explorers' Guild Request Board
variables.description: Current public requests visible on the Explorers' Guild board.
variables.behaviorRules: UI-owned public board cache. Reading/searching the Guild request board populates this directly without sending a narrated chat turn. Rows are offers, not accepted contracts. Shape: {id,title,detail,reward,deadline,minRank,source,status,formal}. This is NOT the adventurer/party search board.

variables.name: Origin
variables.description: Player origin at world entry.
variables.behaviorRules: Fixed campaign premise: the player is an independent transmigrated Evil Spirit from Earth in Bjorn Yandel's era. This does not make NPCs aware of the secret.

variables.name: Dungeon & Stone Familiarity
variables.description: Remembered game familiarity.
variables.behaviorRules: Casual, Experienced, Veteran, Deep Specialist. Affects remembered information only, never raw power/luck/omniscience.

variables.name: Starting Background
variables.description: Starting social circumstances.
variables.behaviorRules: Selected in character creation. A starting social circumstance only; it seeds plausible history, obligations and contacts without granting plot importance.

variables.name: Starting Circumstances
variables.description: Creation snapshot used to seed living-world state.
variables.behaviorRules: Written directly by the creation UI. Seeds district/locality, occupation, social standing, contacts, obligations/debts, affiliations, unregistered explorer status and the body's existing legal situation.

variables.name: Hunger
variables.description: Nourishment reserve.
variables.behaviorRules: Depletes from elapsed time/exertion, not chat turns. Food restores only what is consumed. Low hunger harms recovery/performance; prolonged starvation can reduce condition.

variables.name: Hydration
variables.description: Body hydration.
variables.behaviorRules: Depletes from elapsed time, heat and exertion. Drinking restores only what is physically consumed. Low hydration harms focus/stamina; severe dehydration can reduce condition.

variables.name: Carry State
variables.description: Derived physical carrying load and burden bands.
variables.behaviorRules: DERIVED from actual carried/equipped item weights. Capacity is a simulation abstraction based primarily on Physique plus live strength substat/essence modifiers and race/body multiplier. Canon does not publish a universal carry-weight formula. Use comfortable/heavy/overloaded/immobile bands. Backpacks provide finite organization/storage/access, not supernatural lifting strength.

variables.name: Item Use Ledger
variables.description: Recent deterministic item effects.
variables.behaviorRules: UI-owned audit trail keyed to stable item id and clock.

variables.name: Registered Vault Balance
variables.description: Currency physically lodged in the player's registered Alminus account.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE/UI-OWNED. Changed only by the Alminus counter interface or repair channel. This is separate from the unregistered box.

variables.name: Unregistered Box Balance
variables.description: Currency physically lodged in the password-only unregistered Alminus box.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE/UI-OWNED. Changed only by the Alminus counter interface or repair channel. No identity is attached to this balance.

variables.name: Registered Box Items
variables.description: Physical objects lodged in the registered Alminus deposit box.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE/UI-OWNED. Stable physical item ids must be preserved. Items here cannot be worn, used, sold or carried until withdrawn at an Alminus counter.

variables.name: Unregistered Box Items
variables.description: Physical objects lodged in the password-only unregistered Alminus box.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE/UI-OWNED. Stable physical item ids must be preserved. No identity is attached to this box. Items here cannot be worn, used, sold or carried until withdrawn at an Alminus counter.

variables.name: Alminus Vault Access
variables.description: Account-opening and access metadata. The unregistered password is stored only as a UI hash, never as the password text.
variables.behaviorRules: UI-OWNED. registeredOpen/registeredHeir describe the named account. unregisteredOpen/unregisteredPasswordHash describe the anonymous password-only box. Never narrate, expose, infer or print the password or hash. The actual password exists only in player UI input.

variables.name: Human Kill Count
variables.description: Generic count of sapient/explorer-race people personally killed by the player, regardless of race.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE-OWNED. Increment once for every person killed by the player when isPerson:true, regardless of whether the victim is Human, Barbarian, Dwarf, Fairy, Beastman, Draconian, or another sapient/explorer race. This is a generic HUMAN/PERSON kill counter only. It gives no achievement points, essence roll, mana stone, or bestiary species credit. Robbing, defeating, knocking unconscious, or leaving someone alive does not count.

variables.name: Physical Loot Resolution Ledger
variables.description: Idempotency ledger preventing the same defeated person's physical loot, carried currency, or death from being paid twice.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE-OWNED. Keys are stable person/loot event ids. Each value may contain loot:true, stones:true, kill:true. Once a flag is true, that physical consequence has already been applied and must never be applied again, even if the same death/robbery is later reported through another channel. This ledger is bookkeeping only and is never narrated.

variables.name: Market Index
variables.description: Engine-owned local price/supply indices by commodity category and district.
variables.behaviorRules: Engine-owned economic state. 1.0 is normal. Values move only from causal supply/demand/world events and mean-revert gradually. Never change merely because the player entered a shop.

variables.name: Commodity Ledger
variables.description: Persistent supply/demand shocks and market-relevant flows.
variables.behaviorRules: Record meaningful economic flows, shortages, surpluses, production disruptions and large purchases/sales. Do not record every loaf. Each event should include category, direction, magnitude, locality, cause and day.

variables.name: Economic History
variables.description: Compact history of meaningful market movements and their causes.
variables.behaviorRules: Keep only economically meaningful changes. Prices require causal explanation. Public knowledge depends on information routes.

variables.name: Service Market
variables.description: Current baseline service/labor rates and local multipliers.
variables.behaviorRules: Derived from skill, time, danger, material inputs, scarcity, district and reputation. Canon exact prices override simulation.

variables.name: Economy Day
variables.description: Monotonic economy tick/day used for deterministic market updates.
variables.behaviorRules: Advance only with actual elapsed world time; never because a screen is opened.

variables.name: World Needs
variables.description: Persistent unresolved needs that can cause Guild requests, shortages, procurement and other work.
variables.behaviorRules:
Each row is a real unmet need, not a quest: {id,kind,category,locality,cause,target,quantity,urgency,economicStake,status,createdDay,linkedRequestIds}. Needs arise from actual world/economic conditions and can be solved by the player, NPCs, organizations, or by the cause disappearing.

WORLD-LAW PREVALIDATION: A need inside protected Rafdonia may not use an ordinary Labyrinth monster as cause/target unless a matching active city-monster-incidents record already exists from an independently established extraordinary event. Invalid needs are cancelled and guildEligible=false.

variables.name: Guild Request Ledger
variables.description: Persistent causal links between Guild postings and the real world need/employer behind them.
variables.behaviorRules: Preserve requestId, needId, employer, rewardBasis, acceptedBy, status and outcome. Requests do not exist merely because the player opened the board.

variables.name: Monster Drop Catalog
variables.description: Known species-specific physical byproducts and harvesting facts.
variables.behaviorRules: Canon-established drops/byproducts are authoritative. Mana stones and essence mechanics stay separate. If canon is silent, only plausible mundane byproducts may be simulated and must remain fixed once instantiated.

variables.name: Monster Loot Ledger
variables.description: Physical monster byproducts harvested from specific corpse events.
variables.behaviorRules: Tracks event ID, species, harvested item IDs and resolution so the same corpse cannot pay physical byproducts twice.

variables.name: Ground / World Items
variables.description: Physical items not currently carried because they were dropped, spilled, cached, disarmed or left somewhere.
variables.behaviorRules: Keep stable item identity, location and context. Dropped objects do not follow the player.

variables.name: Narrative Ingest Requests
variables.description: Engine queue for explicit typed attempts to eat/drink a real carried item.
variables.behaviorRules: When the player explicitly types that they eat or drink a specific item they physically possess, push one request: {id,action:'eat'|'drink',itemId?,itemName?,amount?,status:'pending'}. Do not directly remove the item or alter hunger/hydration in narration. The UI engine resolves the request against stable inventory identity, physical accessibility, portions/container contents, and applies the same deterministic consumption logic as the EAT/DRINK buttons. Never create a request for hypothetical speech, questions, plans, or an item the player does not possess.

variables.name: Party Combat Events
variables.description: Engine queue for injuries/damage/status/death affecting persistent party members.
variables.behaviorRules: When combat narration establishes that a persistent party member is actually hit, healed by a non-engine source, injured, knocked down, killed, or receives/loses a status, append ONE unresolved event. Shape: {id, memberId?, memberName, type:'damage|heal|injury|status|death|recover', amount?, injury?, status?, resolved:false}. Do not directly write the party variable. Do not invent an event merely because combat exists; it must correspond to an outcome actually established in narration.

variables.name: Party Progression Events
variables.description: Queue for real companion item and essence progression that must persist into the party roster.
variables.behaviorRules: Append ONE unresolved event only after narration establishes the physical/soul event. Shape: {id, memberId?, memberName, type:'item-gain|item-loss|essence-absorb|essence-erase|essence-capacity', item?, itemId?, essence?, source?, amount?, resolved:false}. For essence-absorb, provide the full established essence object when known: {source,rank,weight,guardian?,abilities,statBoost,statMods}. Essence absorption is permanent until erased and must obey that member's capacity. Never transfer an already absorbed essence between ordinary people as if it were an item. For item-gain/item-loss, only report actual possession changes not already performed by the UI transfer buttons.

variables.name: Party Life Events
variables.description: Optional queue for companion offscreen choices that need narrator-authored consequences beyond the automatic daily surface-life pass.
variables.behaviorRules: Use only for meaningful independently initiated companion choices that the deterministic surface-life pass cannot represent: personal appointments, family obligations, disputes, side work, training commitments, social ties, debts, purchases of a specific established item, or temporarily leaving to handle personal business. Preserve personality and information limits. Do not use it to force companions into the player's plot.

variables.name: Companion Life Directives
variables.description: Narrator-to-engine queue for established companion goals, obligations, relationships, availability, and information disclosure.
variables.behaviorRules: Append unresolved events after the fiction establishes them. Shape: {id,memberId?,memberName,type:'goal-add|goal-complete|obligation-add|relationship|availability|knowledge-reveal|private-knowledge',data,resolved:false}. Use knowledge-reveal only when {{user}} actually learns something. private-knowledge is never automatically player knowledge.
