variables.name: NPC Actor Directives
variables.description: Narrator-to-engine queue for persistent NPC identity, background, stats, personality, inventory, memory, goals, relationships, injuries, schedules and knowledge.
variables.behaviorRules:
Whenever fiction establishes a durable fact about a named/materially relevant NPC, append an unresolved event. Shape: {id,actorId?,name?,type:'upsert|memory|goal-add|goal-complete|obligation-add|relationship|knowledge|knowledge-reveal|inventory-gain|inventory-loss|damage|heal|status|location|availability|sim-level|recruitment',data,resolved:false}. Use upsert.data for established fields such as race, age, role/occupation, affiliation, background, personality, stats, skills, essences, home, personalStones, goals, scheduleState. Do not invent canon facts when unknown. Generated numeric stats/personality are simulation adapters and hidden from the player unless an in-world method reveals them.
For type:'recruitment', data={status:'negotiating|eligible|recruited|declined|withdrawn',terms?,notes?}. Prefer recruitment-events for normal consent.

variables.name: NPC Interaction Ledger
variables.description: Persistent identity-addressed record of meaningful player↔NPC interactions for memory continuity.
variables.behaviorRules: Append concise events only when a named NPC personally witnesses/interacts with {{user}}: conversation, promise, insult, favor, threat, trade, injury, recruitment offer, etc. Include actorId/name and what that NPC could actually know.

variables.name: Labyrinth Entry Window
variables.description: Runtime state for Rafdonia's monthly ordinary Labyrinth entry gate.
variables.behaviorRules: Compatibility timing config only. Authoritative portal state comes from surface-time. Day 1 00:00–00:59 accepts entry; at/after ~01:00 CLOSED until next month.

variables.name: Rift Portal Rules
variables.description: Canon-aware portal behavior registry; prevents one portal subtype's rule from becoming universal.
variables.behaviorRules: Statue-activated guardian portals in the researched later stone chamber close after 10 minutes if nobody enters. Do not apply this universally. Portal capacity/use behavior must follow the specific rift: designated-entrant portals, one-time-use portals, permanent portals, and special guardian portals can differ.

variables.name: Canon Authority Registry
variables.description: Master classification and precedence contract separating canon laws, initial canon state, reference lore, simulation inferences, and playthrough-generated state.

CANON_LAW.meaning: Mechanically consequential canon rule/law. Binding unless canon itself supplies an exception or causally changed state makes the premise inapplicable.

CANON_STATE.meaning: Established world fact at the campaign's historical point. Authoritative initialization, but can change through causal play.

CANON_REFERENCE.meaning: Descriptive, cultural, historical, atmospheric, visual, or explanatory lore used for faithful portrayal but not a runtime constraint by itself.

PROCEDURAL_STATE.meaning: Persistent facts created by this campaign's causal history: purchases, injuries, relationships, deaths, discovered places, changed prices, etc.

SIMULATION_INFERENCE.meaning: A mechanical value/rule needed by the RPG that canon does not specify exactly. Must be labeled and must yield to later/stronger canon.

variables.behaviorRules: Treat the authority class as binding metadata. Never silently upgrade inference/reference into canon law. Never let descriptive prose override a canon law or established causal state. If sources conflict or an exact value is unsupported, preserve uncertainty rather than inventing canon.

variables.name: Canon State Overrides
variables.description: Persistent causal changes to initial canon state produced by this campaign.
variables.behaviorRules: Only store state changes that actually occurred in play or were established by an authoritative campaign event. This does not rewrite canon history globally; it records this playthrough's divergence.

variables.name: Procedural World State
variables.description: Persistent campaign-generated facts not supplied by canon.
variables.behaviorRules: Use for generated people, possessions, relationships, discoveries, local events and other causal facts. Procedural state must respect canon law and existing canon state unless play has causally changed that state.

variables.name: Labyrinth Entry Gate State
variables.description: Compatibility mirror of authoritative physical ordinary Labyrinth entrance state.
variables.behaviorRules: Mirror surface-time-derived physical state only. Never infer from narration, floor duration, or NPC statements.

variables.name: Surface Time
variables.description: Canonical Rafdonia/world-surface calendar clock. Only this clock controls surface dates, schedules, monthly Labyrinth entry availability, and surface NPC catch-up.
variables.behaviorRules: Derived canonical surface date/time mirror. `clock` is numeric minutes since midnight and cycle-day/cycle-month supply the date. This mirror must not parse clock as HH:MM text. Surface NPC/companion catch-up uses this clock domain only, never Labyrinth subjective time.

variables.name: Labyrinth Time
variables.description: Subjective expedition clock for people physically inside the Labyrinth.
variables.behaviorRules: Controls lived time, hunger, thirst, fatigue, sleep, supplies, injuries, training, and floor closure. Never directly advances surface time.

variables.name: Labyrinth Physical State
variables.description: Authoritative physical state of the ordinary Rafdonia Labyrinth entrance.
variables.behaviorRules: World truth, not NPC belief. When exists=false, narration may not depict the ordinary entrance portal as visible, active, or accepting explorers.

variables.name: Recruitment Events
variables.description: Narrator-to-engine queue for recruitment consent and withdrawal by persistent NPCs.
variables.behaviorRules: Append ONE event whenever a named NPC materially changes their answer about joining the player's party. Shape: {id,actorId?,name,type:'offer|eligible|declined|withdrawn',terms?,notes?,rank?,race?,age?,class?,resolved:false}. Use type:'eligible' IMMEDIATELY in the same turn an NPC explicitly agrees to join, accepts the offer, shakes on the deal, or otherwise gives clear consent. Do not add them to party directly. The runtime creates the prospect and RECRUIT button. Use declined on refusal and withdrawn if consent is later revoked.

variables.name: City Monster Incidents
variables.description: Explicit causal exceptions where a Labyrinth monster is physically present inside protected Rafdonia.
variables.behaviorRules: Default empty. Never create an incident merely to justify a procedural Guild request. Requires an already-established extraordinary cause such as canon event, dimensional anomaly, deliberate smuggling/release, experiment, or attack. Shape: {id,species,location,cause,evidence,status:'active|resolved',establishedClock}. Ordinary ecology, drains, butcher waste, darkness, vermin, or wandering are NOT valid causes.

variables.name: Paladin's Public Standing
variables.description: Only meaningful if the player holds the Paladin class. Tracks accumulated public standing toward the next Church-granted skill — a wholly different mechanic from the stage/proficiency ladder every other skill uses.
variables.behaviorRules:
PALADIN-ONLY, AND STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER SKILL. This never uses Barely Formed through Sovereign, never uses proficiency-per-stage. It is a single accumulating number that only goes up through real, confirmed action types: killing monsters in the Labyrinth, genuine donations to a denomination, or completing an actual Church-assigned mission. Raise it by a real, proportionate amount for a real action — never for training, never for time passing.

THE GRANT IS A CEREMONY, NOT A THRESHOLD TICK. Once standing has clearly accumulated, the Pope — or a suitable ranking Church figure if the Pope is narratively unavailable — has to actually appear and hold a real prayer ceremony in the fiction. Only THAT scene, not the number alone, produces a new granted skill/ability, and it happens on the Church's own schedule, not the player's. Never auto-grant a new Paladin ability just because the number crossed some round value — the ceremony has to be played out.

This variable means nothing for a non-Paladin character — don't touch it for anyone else.

variables.name: Noble Contact Ledger
variables.description: The real gate on noble interaction — which named houses have actually made contact, and how.
variables.behaviorRules:
THIS IS THE GATE. reputation.<house> means nothing for a named noble house until a real contact scene has actually happened and been pushed here first. Fame and titles alone don't make a noble's reputation.* entry valid — a genuine scene does.

Push only after a real, narrated first contact:
[noble-contacts: push {"house": "Countess of Alminus", "firstContact": "cycle 5, day 12", "note": "summoned after the Alminus Exchange appraisal made her aware of the piece"}]

WHAT TRIGGERS A REAL CONTACT OPPORTUNITY — this has to be earned, the same way Bjorn's own noble contact grew out of real feats, not simply existing: fame crossing a real threshold combined with something that would actually draw a SPECIFIC house's attention (a title that fits their known interests, a feat touching their business — Alminus notices rare items moving through her Exchange, Kealunus notices clan-affecting Labyrinth feats, Melves notices anything that touches the multiracial political tension they already live inside). Never generate a noble invitation from a generic fame number alone — it has to connect to a SPECIFIC named house for a SPECIFIC, stated reason.

ONCE CONTACT IS REAL, IT'S REAL — a house that has met the player doesn't forget them, and reputation.<house> becomes a genuine, trackable, persistent relationship from that point on: an invitation to a tournament as a guest, a request for audience, a commission, a warning. Nobility attention is exactly as double-edged as fame itself — being noticed by a named house is also being noticed, period, and should push suspicion the same way any sudden visibility does. This is a real, earnable path, not background scenery — treat it as reachable, the way it genuinely was for the one Barbarian who ever managed it.

variables.name: Rift Cycle State
variables.description: Engine-owned. Which of the 13 named rifts are actually open this cycle, resolved by real dice, not GM narration.
variables.behaviorRules: ENGINE-OWNED — you never set this directly; RiftCycle resolves it the instant a new monthly cycle begins. Before narrating whether ANY named rift (Bloody Citadel, Glacial Cave, Green Coal Mine, Steel Tomb, Gunpo/Rocky Desert, White Temple, Doppelganger Forest, Fortress of the Soul, Island of Paradise, Balantis, Calhaem, Red Dragon's Heart, Third Archive) is open, findable, or worth searching for — CHECK THIS FIRST. A rift marked open only becomes physically reachable from cycle-day 4 onward (accessibleFromDay), matching the 'needs three real days to generate' rule. A rift not listed as open this cycle stays closed no matter how convenient the story beat would be — don't invent an exception.

variables.name: Racial State
variables.description: The character's own race's system only: imprint stage, aura, contracts or Soul Tree. Set at creation; drawn as one race-specific sheet tab.
variables.behaviorRules: Set by the interface at creation; never rebuild it. Merge fields, never replace the object. It holds hidden truths (Human aura.talent, Beastman soulTree.chosen) that stay secret until revealed in the fiction. See the 'Racial State' entry for what each field means and when it may change.

description: A persistent sandbox simulation of Rafdonia during Bjorn Yandel's era. Dungeon & Stone mechanics operate as the underlying laws of a physically lived world. The player is an independent transmigrated Evil Spirit who chooses their own life rather than following a main plot. NPCs and organizations persist offscreen; economy, politics, rumors, events, prices, world state, and historical divergence change through causal consequences grounded in the novel/world lore.
